"You..." Skarn whipped toward the dogkin lord, his fury stripped of anything diplomatic. "Your daughter is being bred by the Villain and you expect us to trust your counsel?!"
From the dogkin ranks, a single hand rose with a middle finger extended so gracefully it could have been a royal wave.

"I'm not being 'bred' by anyone, thank you very much," Kitsara announced, her red eyes bright with theatrical indignation. "I'll have you know that I'm a delicate lady adored by her mate for her wonderful personality, not a baby-pumping machine."
Despite her words and extended middle finger, Kitsara didn't seem particularly offended.
She just corrected what was factually wrong.
After all, Quinlan hadn't even 'bred' her a single time!
They were just fucking like depraved rabbits basically every single night.
However, unlike the Slutty Foxy, Vargis did take serious offense.
Whatever warmth had been in his voice was gone.

"You will address my daughter with the respect I extend toward you and your family." His gaze held Skarn's without wavering. "I have betrayed nothing. I merely suggested that entering a war against the combined forces of the Primordial Villain, Vraven, the dwarves, and the elves simultaneously might warrant more than two minutes of thought."
Gorruk's massive arms unfolded, and every lord on the beastkin side felt it.

"Vargis is right." His eyes settled on Skarn, then Rajah, and held. "The fury is earned. I won't pretend otherwise. But the army to back it up isn't standing behind you right now, and you both know it."
Neither lord answered.
"We go home. We rebuild. And when we return to this conversation, we come from strength instead of fumes."
Skarn didn't respond.
His grey eyes locked onto Quinlan.

sentences.text: "Do they really go home... to their families?"
Before anyone could even respond, Elisabeth Valorian looked at the soul formation.
The answer was in every face she found.
The blue-skinned soldier's fists were still shaking but his feet were planted, his tears dried to streaks.
The young woman clutched her own arms, white-knuckled.
The soldier who had spoken about his mother had raised his head and was staring at Elisabeth without a word, and none of them needed one.
They did go home to their families.
When Elisabeth finally spoke again, her voice carried a tremor she couldn't quite steady.
"I will need to convene with the heads of the clergy." She steadied herself on the second sentence, finding footing in procedure.
"A matter of this magnitude cannot be decided on a battlefield or by myself alone.
The church must pray, seek the Goddess's guidance, and reach a consensus before any position is taken."
"Why don't you just ask her?"
Quinlan's tone made it sound like the most reasonable question in the world.
His helmeted head tilted.
"I'm ready to hear her decree right now."
Elisabeth stared at him, uncertain if she should entertain the question.
Then she exhaled, strained, and reluctantly answered.
"The Goddess is greatly limited in what she can and cannot do, even when it comes to conversing with her chosen." Her eyes fell.
"She has never spoken to me when I wasn't near one of her holy sanctuaries."
'Hmm...' Quinlan filed that away without a second thought.
"But aren't you a special case?
Unlike the other Arch Priestesses, you can call upon her powers far from any church."
Her chin rose, and the stubbornness that settled over her expression would have been more intimidating if it didn't also make her look like she was pouting.
"I spoke more than enough to you already, Villain.
The workings of the Goddess's church and the nature of her blessed powers are not topics I intend to discuss with a necro-"
She paused, looked at the petite samurai who was still staring at her, coughed into her palms, and corrected herself.
"Necromancer."
Although it wasn't evident in spoken language, everyone present understood what she'd just done.
She paused to use capital N instead of lowercase for 'Necromancer'.
Ayame's satisfaction multiplied tenfold.
The samurai's victorious expression seemed to have a direct correlation with the degree to which Elisabeth's lips pouted.
A low chuckle rolled through Quinlan's helmet at her refusal to humor him.
"Alright."
He let the sound die, then spoke as if the thought had just occurred to him.
"Why don't you come with us, then?
I'll need to speak with your father regardless, and I'd like to do it in one of my settlements.
There's a church of the Goddess in one of them, so you can speak to her in proper sanctity.
You can also see for yourself how my summons live with their families while you're at it."
The words settled over the field, and for one breath nobody moved.
"WHAT!" Elisabeth released an unladylike shriek, her head snapping toward him so hard her golden hair whipped her in the face.
"You have a church of the Goddess?!" The cry came out strangled.
"You?!"
The disbelief wasn't hers alone.
A shockwave of voices broke across the field.
In the elven ranks, officers looked to each other, wide-eyed.
Human soldiers shouted over one another, and somewhere in the crowd a voice rose above the rest:
"The Villain has a church?!"
The Primordial Villain, the Necromancer, the armored figure who commanded legions of the dead and bore a title synonymous with evil, had allowed a house of worship to exist in his lands?
Did he fund its construction?!
Why would he do such a thing?!
Who was leading the clergy?!
Was it some Goddess-forsaken heretical representation of their holy sanctuary?!
So many questions rippled through the crowd.
Elisabeth's head swung to her father, and her expression screamed a question she couldn't bring herself to voice.
'Did you know?!'
Alexios's face told her all she needed to know.
He had no fucking idea.
"What city?" Alexios demanded, irritation and incredulity plain in his tone.
"You shouldn't have any cities."
Quinlan's gaze shifted to the king of Vraven, and the silence he offered in return was so smugly unhelpful it might as well have been a wink.
Behind Quinlan, Myrasyn's ears shot straight up and her hands clasped together in front of her chest, the elven queen's composure fracturing into an eagerness she couldn't have hidden if she'd tried.

Her green eyes darted toward Quinlan, bright and expectant, already calculating how to include herself in that invitation to visit his personal domain and see just what sort of rulership the Holy Son utilized.

chapters.title: Chapter 1768 Ayame's Realization
paragraphs: The glare that burned behind them carried every ounce of wounded pride and predatory fury the wolfkin lord had swallowed since the negotiations began.
He held it there, seconds stretching, turning heavier, as if sheer will could convey the promise his words weren't allowed to make.
Then he scoffed, sharp and guttural, and turned his back on the armored figure.
"This is a grave mistake!" The snarl tore across the field as Skarn stalked away, his grey fur still bristling.
Rajah's amber gaze lingered on Quinlan for a beat longer than Skarn's had, cold and measuring, before the tigerkin lord turned and followed without a word.
Quinlan watched them go, then looked at Gorruk.

The bearkin lord seemed to be the one all of them listened to. At least somewhat... Vargis was not only a dogkin, a tribe not counted among the apexes of the beastkin, but he also had familial ties to Quinlan.
All of this made Gorruk the one worth talking to.
"I'll reach out soon to iron out the details," Quinlan said. "You have my word."
Gorruk nodded toward the armored figure, a slow dip that carried the weight of a handshake between men who didn't quite trust each other but understood the math.
"We'll take the foxkin with us," Gorruk said, his attention shifting to the disarmed soldiers huddled among the beastkin ranks. "What's left of them falls under the Confederation's jurisdiction."

Quinlan nodded in response. Silver's remnants were a mess the Beastman Confederation would have to sort through on its own, and he had no interest in meddling with their internal politics as long as whatever they decided didn't circle back to bite him.
Gorruk turned without ceremony, and the beastkin withdrawal began.
It wasn't a retreat.
Skarn's wolfkin fell into formation first, moving with the tight discipline of a pack following its alpha regardless of his mood, weapons still drawn and ears flat as they filed away from the field.
Rajah's tigerkin followed in loose, prowling clusters, amber-striped soldiers casting glances over their shoulders at the elven and human ranks as if memorizing faces for a later date.
The dogkin lingered longest.
Vargis gave Quinlan a long, measured look before turning to his soldiers. "Let's move."
Although he visibly would've liked to stay, he had his duties as the tribe's leader.
"Bye-bye everyone!! Thanks for the help!" Kitsara cheered, waving energetically at her people.

The dogkin troops fell in behind Vargis with tails wagging upon hearing the gratuitous words their princess had spoken, and more than a few of them stole glances at Blossom as they passed, ears perked and eyes bright with the same fierce approval their lord had shown during her eruption.

Gorruk's bearkin moved last, massive forms peeling away from the edges of the field in unhurried strides with their lord at the center. Among them, the foxkin prisoners shuffled, disarmed and surrounded, trembling like deer in the headlights.
Four separate columns filed off the flat ground, each tribe keeping its own line and its own pace, and the gaps between them said everything about the state of the Confederation that words hadn't.

A collective exhale rolled through the elven ranks as the last beastkin column disappeared from view, thousands of shoulders dropping at once as the tension that had been coiling since Skarn first snarled at their queen finally bled out of the field.
They had come within a breath of fighting each other, and every elf present knew it.
"She's been stabilized."
Seraphiel's voice arrived from behind Ayame, warm and steady.
The Dawnbringer had been kneeling over Kaede since the negotiations began, golden light fading from her palms as she rose to her feet and dusted off her knees.
Ayame found her sister being lifted off the ground by two elite soul healers, Kaede's body limp and her breathing shallow but even.

The stat loss from the Fujimori blade going inert had turned injuries she could have fought through into ones that put her down, and now she hung between the two souls like a puppet with its strings cut.
Ayame watched them carry her away, and the expression on her face was one that didn't belong to either version of herself.
Not the composed second-in-command, nor the bratty girl.
Just a woman staring at the unconscious body of the sister who had sold her and ruined her life, not knowing what to do with any of it.
A hand landed on her shoulder, heavy and warm.
"You have all the time in the world," Quinlan said, his armored fingers squeezing once. "No need to rush anything."
Ayame exhaled slowly, the tension leaving her frame in stages, and nodded. "Yeah. I know."
Quinlan's visor lingered on her for a beat, then the fire behind it shifted. The helmet receded until his face was bare for the world to see, showing a smirk. "Tell me, how was it?"
Ayame turned to look at him, and the grin that spread across her face was the most satisfied expression she had worn all day.
"Roasting the priestess?" She tilted her head, savoring the words. "It was phenomenal."
"WHAT?!" Elisabeth's shriek nearly took their eardrums out. After all, she was only a step or so away. "I'm still right here, you know! Only the beastkin left!"

Ayame didn't so much as glance in her direction. She shook her head, still grinning, and her voice carried the lightness of a fresh discovery, the kind of universal truth that left her amused beyond belief.

"I've learned something new today, Quin. If you have a gullible little sister who sold you into slavery and almost ruined your entire life because she was too easy to manipulate, all you really need is an Arch Priestess to use as an emotional punching bag and suddenly everything feels just a bit brighter."
"HAH?!" Elisabeth's voice cracked on the syllable, her face cycling through so many shades of red it was almost impressive.
Myrasyn covered her mouth with both hands, but the laugh escaped through her fingers anyway.
It was new to all listeners, the heretical behavior these people showed toward the Goddess and her chosen. Though they had to admit, listening to them had been anything but boring.
In the elven ranks, thousands of ears twitched in sync, hoping they could hear more from these people who bashed the hypocrite priestess with so little restraint.
As the woman in question kept harrumphing about sacrilege and the like, Seraphiel began giggling into her palm and Vex's cackle followed.
Despite the rising tide of overlapping voices, Quinlan's chuckle was the loudest of them all.
His gauntlet came up and ran through Ayame's lush black hair, slow and fond. "Well said."
"VILLAIN!" Elisabeth stamped her foot, golden hair flying. "I can HEAR you!"
Nobody cared.
Quinlan let the laughter settle around him, his fingers still in Ayame's hair, and his gaze drifted to the horizon where the beastkin columns were shrinking into the distance.
It was time to move on.
He had settlements to show to his new guests and a church for the Arch Priestess to lose her mind over.
And after that, it would finally be time to crack open the secrets the Fujimori clan had been hoarding for generations.

chapters.title: Chapter 1769 Bad Move
paragraphs: Quinlan pulled his fingers from Ayame's hair and let the warmth of the moment drain with them, because the field he was standing on was still a warzone.
The laughter had bought everyone a few minutes.
Now those minutes were over, and the list of problems waiting for him stretched longer than the beastkin columns disappearing on the horizon.
Bodies carpeted the ground in overlapping layers, feral undead from the Covenant's shattered horde still stumbling into clusters of wounded soldiers.

The dwarven king sat frozen in a block of ice with no one quite sure what to do with him, and somewhere behind the elven lines, the Fujimori prisoners needed to be secured before they became four different kinds of headache.
He didn't need to say a word.
The tension that had been winding tighter since Skarn first snarled at him was unwinding now, and with it came the part his girls were best at: the work nobody thanked you for.

Ayame had already pulled a cluster of soul officers aside, her bratty energy shelved into the composed noble who ran his affairs when he wasn't looking, and Quinlan could hear her voice carrying across the field as she started coordinating prisoner transfers.
Seraphiel's golden light bloomed a dozen paces to the right, warm and wide, the Dawnbringer kneeling over a wounded elven soldier.
Serika was hauling a collapsed barricade off a pile of bodies with her bare hands.
Nearby, a handful of dwarven prisoners had inched closer and closer to their frozen king when they thought no one was watching, trying to sneak up and free him.
One of them was muttering about structural fault lines and heat application points when Kaelira's long ears twitched.
She walked over, arms folded, and the dwarves went still the moment they registered what was standing in front of them: an elf, towering over them, looking thoroughly unimpressed.
"I told you to keep your voice down!" one of them hissed at the muttering dwarf.
"I was!"
"Clearly not, since the elf heard you from thirty paces!"
Kaelira ignored the bickering and walked all the way up to the ice block housing Ragnar.

Her fingers trailed the frozen surface as a smith's analytical eyes replaced the stalwart tanker's gaze. "Heating the outer shell would cause a thermal shock that fractures inward. His heart stops before the first layer melts."
The dwarves exchanged baffled looks. They'd been caught trying to free their king and the elf was... solving the puzzle for them?
She tilted her head. "Chipping produces vibrations that do the same thing. The ice is elementally reinforced, so brute force won't even scratch it."
An impressed smile replaced her pursed lips as she announced her findings: "The only person getting him out of there safely is the person who put him in."
The dwarves stared at her with mounting confusion.
"Either way," Kaelira said, "I'd sit back down if I were you."
She raised a finger to point over her shoulder without turning around.
A dozen elven soldiers were visible where they'd been standing the entire time, longbows drawn and arrows nocked, their expressions carrying the kind of sweetness that preceded violence.
They'd been watching the dwarves inch toward the ice block from the start, waiting with the patient glee of predators who had been told not to kill the prey unless it gave them a reason.
"Aww... You're no fun!" One of them giggled. Actually giggled, the tip of her arrow still aimed at the nearest dwarf's throat, and the sound was the least reassuring thing any of them had ever heard.
Then, slowly, the bows lowered, and the elven soldiers' expressions twisted into genuine disappointment.
The color had left every dwarven face in the group.
One of them sat down on the frozen ground, not because he wanted to, but because his legs had quit on him.
"T-thank you..." the nearest dwarf managed, his voice thin enough to pass through a keyhole. "Why did you save us, lass?"
Kaelira didn't look at him as she replied with zero emotion. "I have a feeling you'll play an important role in my... partner's future plans." She turned away. "I didn't want you dying just yet."
Yet.
Quinlan shook his head, amused, as he watched it all from the center of the field and felt the knot in his chest loosen.
'They've got this.'
He could leave the cleanup duty to his girls, letting him proceed with what he had in mind.
His gaze drifted to find Black Fang. She stood apart from everyone else with her arms loose at her sides, watching the field with an expression that gave away nothing.
But her eyes said what her face wouldn't.
She had a certain item on her agenda, just didn't want to ask his help.
'How adorable...' Quinlan chuckled inwardly as he opened a [Warp Gate] beside her, pale energy swirling to life. "Will you get the preparations done for me, Black Fang?"
The woman in question was moving before the question mark landed, stepping through the portal without a glance, a nod, or a single word in response.

He chuckled again, shaking his head, then flicked two fingers toward the ice blocks containing Hozumi and Chizuru. The frozen elders slid across the ground on a current of earth and vanished through the gate after her.
"Everyone!" Myrasyn's voice cut across her ranks with the snap of a queen who had made up her mind. "Assist the Holy Son's women. We have a battlefield to clean up!"
The elven army moved as if they'd been waiting for the order.
Thousands of soldiers fanned out across the grounds, energized by the duty rather than burdened by it, seeking out Quinlan's women for direction.

Kitsara seemed to be in her element, waving groups of elven soldiers toward tasks with a cheerful authority that had absolutely no business working as well as it did, though the real directing fell to Lucille, Aurora, and Ayame herself.

Alexios watched the elves move, stroked his beard once, then turned to the armored man at his shoulder. "Stormlord. Represent the kingdom's interests while I'm gone. The Fujimori prisoners are still subjects of the crown."
"Yes, Your Majesty."
"Now then." Quinlan clapped his gauntlets together and faced the remaining leaders as if he were about to give a tour of his favorite restaurant. "Shall we begin?"
"Yeah!" Jasmine appeared beside him, beaming, already bouncing on her heels.
"Me too! Me too!"
Felicity came bounding over from Feng's side, waving both arms, and the sight of her stopped Alexios's next breath.
She was drenched in blood.
Head to toe, soaked through, her purple hair matted flat against her skull and her clothes stained so thoroughly that the original color was a matter of speculation. None of it was hers.
The smile splitting her face was brighter than the sun, and she bounced with the energy of a child who had just discovered the world's best playground.
This was not the princess who had been spirited away from his kingdom.
Alexios stared at his daughter for a long moment, and the concern that crossed his face lasted exactly as long as it took for the warrior king to override the doting father inside.
Alexios blinked. "How are you bloodier than the last time I saw you? The fight is over."
"Not everyone accepted defeat with grace, Father." Felicity replied with an ominous grin that belonged on a battlefield veteran twenty times her age.
For a moment the warrior king didn't know what he was looking at.
This was his youngest. His precious little daughter. The girl who used to cry when a flower wilted.
Then he recognized the look in her eyes, because he'd worn it himself at her age, and the savage grin that split his face was pure pride.
"Good."
Felicity beamed at him, then turned and threw herself at Quinlan with full-body enthusiasm, despite weighing about as much as one of his pauldrons.

She latched onto his armor and squeezed, smearing blood across his chestplate, and the hug was so earnest and so happy that it made the Primordial Villain look like a man being ambushed by his little sister after a long day.
Alexios's grin evaporated in the very same instant.

A ribbon of water coiled off Quinlan's free hand and swept through Felicity's hair while she was still clinging to him, pulling the blood out of the purple strands in a single smooth pass before spiraling down her clothes, her arms, her boots, carrying the grime away and leaving her spotless in seconds.
Felicity looked up at him, smiling. "Thank you!"

Before the old king's expression could finish souring at the terrible sight his eyes were carrying to his brain, Felicity released Quinlan and sprinted across the gap, slamming into her father clean and beaming.

The dwarven king sat frozen in a block of ice with no one quite sure what to do with him, and somewhere behind the elven lines, the Fujimori prisoners needed to be secured before they became four different kinds of headache.
He didn't need to say a word.
The tension that had been winding tighter since Skarn first snarled at him was unwinding now, and with it came the part his girls were best at: the work nobody thanked you for.

Ayame had already pulled a cluster of soul officers aside, her bratty energy shelved into the composed noble who ran his affairs when he wasn't looking, and Quinlan could hear her voice carrying across the field as she started coordinating prisoner transfers.
Seraphiel's golden light bloomed a dozen paces to the right, warm and wide, the Dawnbringer kneeling over a wounded elven soldier.
Serika was hauling a collapsed barricade off a pile of bodies with her bare hands.
Nearby, a handful of dwarven prisoners had inched closer and closer to their frozen king when they thought no one was watching, trying to sneak up and free him.
One of them was muttering about structural fault lines and heat application points when Kaelira's long ears twitched.
She walked over, arms folded, and the dwarves went still the moment they registered what was standing in front of them: an elf, towering over them, looking thoroughly unimpressed.
"I told you to keep your voice down!" one of them hissed at the muttering dwarf.
"I was!"
"Clearly not, since the elf heard you from thirty paces!"
Kaelira ignored the bickering and walked all the way up to the ice block housing Ragnar.
Her fingers trailed the frozen surface as a smith's analytical eyes replaced the stalwart tanker's gaze.
"Heating the outer shell would cause a thermal shock that fractures inward.
His heart stops before the first layer melts."
The dwarves exchanged baffled looks.
They'd been caught trying to free their king and the elf was... solving the puzzle for them?
She tilted her head.
"Chipping produces vibrations that do the same thing.
The ice is elementally reinforced, so brute force won't even scratch it."
An impressed smile replaced her pursed lips as she announced her findings: "The only person getting him out of there safely is the person who put him in."
The dwarves stared at her with mounting confusion.
"Either way," Kaelira said, "I'd sit back down if I were you."
She raised a finger to point over her shoulder without turning around.
A dozen elven soldiers were visible where they'd been standing the entire time, longbows drawn and arrows nocked, their expressions carrying the kind of sweetness that preceded violence.
They'd been watching the dwarves inch toward the ice block from the start, waiting with the patient glee of predators who had been told not to kill the prey unless it gave them a reason.
"Aww...
You're no fun!" One of them giggled.
Actually giggled, the tip of her arrow still aimed at the nearest dwarf's throat, and the sound was the least reassuring thing any of them had ever heard.
Then, slowly, the bows lowered, and the elven soldiers' expressions twisted into genuine disappointment.
The color had left every dwarven face in the group.
One of them sat down on the frozen ground, not because he wanted to, but because his legs had quit on him.
"T-thank you..." the nearest dwarf managed, his voice thin enough to pass through a keyhole.
"Why did you save us, lass?"
Kaelira didn't look at him as she replied with zero emotion.
"I have a feeling you'll play an important role in my... partner's future plans." She turned away.
"I didn't want you dying just yet."
Yet.
Quinlan shook his head, amused, as he watched it all from the center of the field and felt the knot in his chest loosen.
'They've got this.'
He could leave the cleanup duty to his girls, letting him proceed with what he had in mind.
His gaze drifted to find Black Fang.
She stood apart from everyone else with her arms loose at her sides, watching the field with an expression that gave away nothing.
But her eyes said what her face wouldn't.
She had a certain item on her agenda, just didn't want to ask his help.
'How adorable...' Quinlan chuckled inwardly as he opened a [Warp Gate] beside her, pale energy swirling to life.
"Will you get the preparations done for me, Black Fang?"
The woman in question was moving before the question mark landed, stepping through the portal without a glance, a nod, or a single word in response.
He chuckled again, shaking his head, then flicked two fingers toward the ice blocks containing Hozumi and Chizuru.
The frozen elders slid across the ground on a current of earth and vanished through the gate after her.
"Everyone!" Myrasyn's voice cut across her ranks with the snap of a queen who had made up her mind.
"Assist the Holy Son's women.
We have a battlefield to clean up!"
The elven army moved as if they'd been waiting for the order.
Thousands of soldiers fanned out across the grounds, energized by the duty rather than burdened by it, seeking out Quinlan's women for direction.

Kitsara seemed to be in her element, waving groups of elven soldiers toward tasks with a cheerful authority that had absolutely no business working as well as it did, though the real directing fell to Lucille, Aurora, and Ayame herself.
Alexios watched the elves move, stroked his beard once, then turned to the armored man at his shoulder.
"Stormlord.
Represent the kingdom's interests while I'm gone.
The Fujimori prisoners are still subjects of the crown."
"Yes, Your Majesty."
"Now then." Quinlan clapped his gauntlets together and faced the remaining leaders as if he were about to give a tour of his favorite restaurant.
"Shall we begin?"
"Yeah!" Jasmine appeared beside him, beaming, already bouncing on her heels.
"Me too!
Me too!"
Felicity came bounding over from Feng's side, waving both arms, and the sight of her stopped Alexios's next breath.
She was drenched in blood.
Head to toe, soaked through, her purple hair matted flat against her skull and her clothes stained so thoroughly that the original color was a matter of speculation.
None of it was hers.
The smile splitting her face was brighter than the sun, and she bounced with the energy of a child who had just discovered the world's best playground.
This was not the princess who had been spirited away from his kingdom.
Alexios stared at his daughter for a long moment, and the concern that crossed his face lasted exactly as long as it took for the warrior king to override the doting father inside.
Alexios blinked.
"How are you bloodier than the last time I saw you?
The fight is over."
"Not everyone accepted defeat with grace, Father." Felicity replied with an ominous grin that belonged on a battlefield veteran twenty times her age.
For a moment the warrior king didn't know what he was looking at.
This was his youngest.
His precious little daughter.
The girl who used to cry when a flower wilted.
Then he recognized the look in her eyes, because he'd worn it himself at her age, and the savage grin that split his face was pure pride.
"Good."
Felicity beamed at him, then turned and threw herself at Quinlan with full-body enthusiasm, despite weighing about as much as one of his pauldrons.

She latched onto his armor and squeezed, smearing blood across his chestplate, and the hug was so earnest and so happy that it made the Primordial Villain look like a man being ambushed by his little sister after a long day.
Alexios's grin evaporated in the very same instant.

A ribbon of water coiled off Quinlan's free hand and swept through Felicity's hair while she was still clinging to him, pulling the blood out of the purple strands in a single smooth pass before spiraling down her clothes, her arms, her boots, carrying the grime away and leaving her spotless in seconds.
Felicity looked up at him, smiling.
"Thank you!"

Before the old king's expression could finish souring at the terrible sight his eyes were carrying to his brain, Felicity released Quinlan and sprinted across the gap, slamming into her father clean and beaming.

chapters.title: Chapter 1770 Crazy Women
paragraphs: Alexios caught her, and the old king's arms closed around his daughter with a gentleness that didn't match his reputation.
She'd hugged the Primordial Villain first.
Then sprinted straight into the arms of the King of Vraven.
The same girl, the same warmth, handed to two men who had been trying to kill each other for months as if loving both of them was the most natural thing in the world.
Felicity pulled back from the hug, still glowing, and seemed to remember something. She cupped her hands around her mouth with the casual tone of someone calling a cat out from under the couch.
"Mother! Come out! It's time to go sightseeing!"
The ground rumbled.

A section of frozen earth split open twenty paces away, and Queen Morgana rose from beneath it on a pillar of compressed stone, her dark purple hair plastered to her face with mud, her enchanted gown caked in filth, and her iridescent eyes burning with enough hatred to melt the ice off the dwarven king's block.
She looked ready to kill someone. Several someones, possibly, starting with the armored figure at the center of this little gathering.
"Did the whole royal family have fun today?" Quinlan asked pleasantly.
Morgana's glare could have curdled milk.
"VILLAIN!" Elisabeth's shriek arrived right on schedule, the Arch Priestess storming forward with golden hair flying. "What have you done to my mother?! She's covered in filth!"

"I parked her underground so she wouldn't cause problems during the negotiations." Quinlan shrugged dismissively, saying it the way someone would explain where they'd left their coat. "Worked out great, actually."
"You buried the Queen of Vraven like a dirt mole?! How dare you?!"
"She's my conquered enemy. Her life is in my hands," Quinlan explained nonchalantly.

Elisabeth looked ready to strangle him with her bare hands, golden light and divine mandate be damned. "Tell me," she managed through her teeth, "that you have a good reason for burying my mother alive."
"Yeah." Quinlan looked at Elisabeth wryly. "I'm looking at it."
"...What?"
"If I'd let you meet her earlier, you would've still been screeching at me about necromancy, slavery, the Goddess's will, and who knows what else instead of actually listening to what I had to say."
He gestured vaguely at the field around them. "But look at us now. The beastkin are leaving, reparations are on the table, everything is moving forward. Isn't it great?"
Elisabeth's fists shook at her sides.
Then her head snapped around, eyes scanning the field until they found Ayame directing soul officers in the distance.
"That girl!" The Arch Priestess's voice cracked. "She told me to go find my mother while knowing she was buried the entire time?!"
"Yeah," Quinlan confirmed, thoroughly unbothered. "She wanted to see you run around like a headless chicken."
"You're the devil!"
"Yeah, that's my criminal alias."
Elisabeth went quiet. The golden light around her flickered once, twice, and the Arch Priestess looked at Quinlan with calm, measured fury. The screaming was over. She was planning now.
"I will remember every single thing you've done today, Villain. Every. Single. Thing."
"Okay," Quinlan nodded.
While Elisabeth visibly restrained herself from committing a cardinal sin on a battlefield, Alexios spoke up.
"Are you alright, Morgana?" His voice was tired and flat.
Morgana turned her blazing eyes on her husband. Animosity burned in them, raw and genuine, directed at him with the same intensity she'd been aiming at Quinlan.
"Shut your mouth."

Alexios blinked. His hand paused mid-stroke on his beard, and for a brief moment the King of Vraven looked like a man genuinely trying to figure out what he'd done wrong by asking his wife if she was alright.
He opened his mouth, reconsidered, closed it, then stroked his beard once and turned away. "...Okay."
She'd been like this before he lost her. She'd been like this after.
Buried in mud, enslaved, humiliated in front of three armies, and still the same cold, hostile woman who'd rather bite the hand reaching for her than take it.
At some point a man simply stops reaching.
Morgana stood rooted in her pillar of mud, staring at the back of her husband's head as he walked away from her.
"Hah?! Hello?!" Her voice cracked with disbelief. "Don't you dare move on just like that!"
Alexios kept walking. Didn't turn, didn't slow, and the silence he left behind hit Morgana harder than anything Quinlan had done to her.
Elisabeth was still sputtering about barbarism and Morgana's fury had soured into bewildered offense, and between the two of them they were generating enough hostile energy to power a small city.
Quinlan glanced sideways at Alexios, grinning.
"You're surrounded by crazy women."
Alexios glanced sideways at Quinlan, exhausted.
"You're one to talk."
"My girls are the good kind of crazy. The sexy crazy. Yours are just batshit insane. No fun in that."
"...Stop badmouthing my wife and daughter."
"Sure."

They then simply turned their backs on the screeching mother-daughter duo and headed toward the spot where the [Warp Gate] was about to open, two men who had absolutely nothing in common except a shared understanding that engaging further was a waste of everyone's time.
Jasmine, fingers still laced through his, began hopping along at his side with a smile so wide it crinkled the corners of her eyes.
Felicity fell into step beside Alexios, her small hand finding his, and the old king let her take it without comment.
From opposite sides of the procession, Jasmine and Felicity caught each other's eyes.

The governor and the freshly cleaned princess stared at each other for a beat, then broke into matching grins so bright and so giddy that the contrast with the two furious women seething behind them could not have been more comical.
Myrasyn glided into formation with Isveth a half-step behind, the elven queen's ears perked and her posture radiating an eagerness she wasn't even trying to hide.
"I am NOT going anywhere with this scumbag!" Elisabeth announced, planting her feet.
"Church," Quinlan reminded her over his shoulder.
Her foot moved before her mouth could argue with it.
The [Warp Gate] bloomed open ahead of them, and the procession filed through without breaking stride, led by two lithe ladies with long, excitedly twitching ears.
"W-wait! I'm coming too! You didn't even invite your superior, Devil?!"
Maelstrom's voice cracked across the field as the Consortium general broke into a desperate sprint, his legs churning beneath him because the important people were leaving without him.
Quinlan stepped through the gate last and closed it behind him.
The pale energy collapsed into nothing, leaving Maelstrom skidding to a halt on the frozen ground where a portal had been half a second ago, his outstretched hand grasping at empty air.
Behind him, a cluster of elven soldiers snickered.
"Shut it!" Maelstrom whipped around, jabbing a finger at them. "I am the general of the Vesper Consortium, and I will not be laughed at by-"
The snickering stopped.
Every elf within earshot turned to face him at the same time, and the giddy amusement on their faces died so fast it was like watching candles get snuffed out.
What replaced it was cold, flat hostility, thousands of pairs of eyes locking onto the Consortium general with the synchronized precision of predators who had identified prey.

Then, with the kind of unison that had no business existing outside of a temple choir, thousands of elven women opened their mouths at the same time, and what came out was a single deep, ominous, feminine voice that rolled across the frozen ground like a hymn from the throat of an ancient monster.
"The only man who can order us around is the Holy Son. Know your place, human."
Maelstrom's finger lowered on its own. His legs, which had already proven unreliable today, decided they wanted to be somewhere else.

"T-tch...!" He scoffed with whatever dignity he could scrape off the frozen ground and turned his back on the elves, stalking toward his Consortium forces with strides that were trying very hard to not be a retreat.
The elven soldiers watched him leave, then returned to their duties as if nothing had happened.
On the other side of the [Warp Gate], Myrasyn and Isveth had stepped through first.
What greeted them on the other side stole the words from both their lips.
"Oh, Graceful Mother..." they whispered in unison, floored.

chapters.title: Chapter 1771 No War Crimes Please
paragraphs: The [Warp Gate] had deposited them on a snow-covered hill a few hundred meters from New Whisperfield's northern edge, and Myrasyn was squinting before anyone else had even stepped through.
"Isveth." She grabbed the other elf's arm without looking away from the view. "Are those trees inside the city?"

Isveth's eyes narrowed against the winter glare. A settlement of compressed earth buildings stretched across several square kilometers of forest below them, three stories tall with frosted quartz windows and external stone staircases, its roads woven between old-growth oaks and evergreen groves that stood inside the city as though the builders had refused to cut a single one.
"They built around them..." Isveth confirmed, and her grip on her own wrist tightened. "As expected of the Holy Son..."
"And the streets are not snowy at all!" Myrasyn squinted, shading her eyes with one hand.
"Are those... Children?" Isveth said. "Running merrily in the cold winter?"
The rest of the procession filed through behind them.
Alexios emerged with Felicity at his side, and the warrior king's stride slowed as his gaze swept the city.
"The bastard really has a city..."
"When will you call Quinlan by his name?" Felicity giggled.
"When he stops being a bastard."
Elisabeth stepped through next and whatever complaint had been building behind her teeth dissolved into stunned silence.
"What is that?!" she shouted, pointing at the settlement in the distance.
Morgana came next, still caked in mud from her underground imprisonment.
The procession finished by Quinlan and Jasmine, walking hand-in-hand.
The guests might have stood there squinting at the settlement for another hour, but movement along the treeline cut the awe short.
A patrol of soldiers crested the hill from the east in tight formation, weapons drawn, their boots crunching through the snow with a discipline that spoke to orders taken seriously.
They'd registered the new arrivals and closed the distance fast.
This hill was priority target to defend, as enemies could use it to barrage New Whisperfield with cannon fire should it be taken.
As such, patrols were a constant in the area.
"Hands in the air and identify yourselves or we will-!" the commander shouted, but then spotted Jasmine first and faltered. Then he spotted the man beside her. "My Lord?! Governor?!"
Jasmine waved them off. "Stand down, captain. They're our guests."
"Yes!" Fists snapped to chests in salute toward their governor.
The patrol leader's eyes lingered on Quinlan for one more heartbeat before training won out over curiosity, and the soldiers resumed their route without another word.
Jasmine turned back to her guests with a sly smile.
"If we want an authentic experience, we'll need to blend in."

Her gaze then drifted upward to the two-meter-tall armored figure beside her whose silhouette could probably be identified from a kilometer away by anyone on the continent who had ever heard the words 'Primordial Villain.'
She giggled softly. "Well... as much as possible."
"Synchra, let's try our best, shall we?" Quinlan replied, addressing his armor.
Synchra's plates shivered with delight at the task, and the living metal began reshaping with the fussy enthusiasm of a woman who'd just been asked to dress her man for an outing.
Her first attempt was a merchant's traveling coat, deep green with brass buttons and a collar that framed his face rather well.
She held the look for a moment, pleased with herself, but then adjusted the collar, adjusted it again, and apparently decided it was too handsome.
The plates rippled into a second try, becoming a farmer's vest over roughspun, worn belt, rolled sleeves, but she fussed with the hem for two full seconds before scrapping that one too.
The third time, she committed.
Obsidian darkened to rough-spun brown, angular segments softened into the loose folds of a laborer's tunic, greaves melted into cracked leather boots.
She added stains, frayed edges, and a patch on the left knee that looked like it had been there for years.
The outfit looked like it hadn't been washed in a week, and Synchra rippled once with quiet satisfaction, finally content with what she'd made for him.
"Good job."
Quinlan's grin was entirely too pleased for the filthy garb she'd dressed him in.
The guests stared.
Not just at the transformation itself, though the fact that an armor could reshape on command was worth several questions from any smith alive.
What arrested them was that the Primordial Villain, the most dangerous man on the continent, had just voluntarily dressed himself as a pauper.
In a world where a man's station was his armor and no noble would be caught dead in commoner cloth, Quinlan wore it without complaint.

"..." Alexios then looked down at his own golden plate, at the royal crest of Vraven stamped into the breastplate, at armor that was very much incapable of turning into anything other than what it was. "My armor can't do that. You expect me to strip bare or what?"

Quinlan wasted no time, offering an offhanded command while adjusting his garbs: "I know we're enemies, you exhibitionist freak, but I'd appreciate it if you attacked me with honor and not war crimes."
Quinlan flicked two fingers and a second [Warp Gate] bloomed open behind him.
Emily came through first.
The head maid emerged with her hands clasped at her waist, posture straight, hair pinned, apron pressed.
Behind her came Clarisse, dignified and unhurried, then the twins Anna and Beatrice in step, then Dorothy, Eira, Ilde, and Cecile in a line so neat it could have been rehearsed.
Eight women in pressed uniforms, each carrying a leather case or folded bundle under her arm.
These were ordinary women, some young and some weathered, with calloused fingers and builds shaped by hard lives rather than noble schools.

But the precision of their formation, the quiet coordination in how they moved, and the way every one of them stood a little taller upon arriving before their master told a different story than their faces did.
"Master." Emily dipped her head toward Quinlan, then swept her eyes across the assembled royals without so much as a blink. "Congratulations on your victory."
"Much appreciated. Has everything been prepared?"
"Yes, we're ready."
"Capable as always, hmm?" Quinlan's voice carried a warmth the guests hadn't heard from him all day.
"We strive to please!" Emily beamed, and so did the others behind her hearing his praise.
He looked across the eight women, fond and genuine, then turned to the assembled kings and queens.
"Aren't my maids amazing? They worked incredibly hard to become as skilled as they are."

His expression shifted, looking at his guests. "Any insult thrown at them is the equivalent of declaring war on me, got it?" His tone was playful, jestful, yet Anna and Beatrice went scarlet in unison.
Eira ducked her head. Cecile bit her lip and couldn't suppress the smile.
The maids, with some struggle to retain their professionalism, moved.
Chairs were brought out, lightweight and collapsible.
They set them in a half-circle facing the settlement, so the guests could watch the winter city while the work was done.
Brushes, pins, powders, ties, and clothing bundles emerged from the remaining cases with the organized efficiency of kits that had been packed and maintained well before this morning.
"Please sit," Emily asked.
Alexios dropped into his chair first, crossed his legs, and watched the proceedings with mild amusement, too old and too seasoned to find any of this beneath him.
The maid assigned to him, Ilde, began working on his armor straps, and the King of Vraven offered her the same cooperation he would have offered a field medic removing his plate after battle.

"You're all so wonderfully trained," Myrasyn chirped loud enough for all to hear, and the warmth in her voice was immediate and sincere. "Any household would be proud to have such elegant and proper maids."
Every maid in earshot straightened.
These were lowborn women, former captives, former nobodies, and a four-thousand-year-old elven queen had just told them they were wonderful.
The pride that rippled through the group was visible in lifted chins and brightened eyes across the line.
Eira's hands trembled as she began undoing Myrasyn's braids, replacing them with something simpler that wouldn't turn every head in the city below.
The young maid's fingers were careful and slow, hyperaware of every strand of the elven queen's hair.
"What's your name, dear?" Myrasyn asked, tilting her head to give the girl better access.
"E-Eira, Your Majesty."
"How long have you served your master, Eira?"
Eira paused. "Umm..."
Her hands stilled in Myrasyn's hair, and her gaze drifted upward toward the winter sun hanging low over the treeline.
She studied its position for a moment, lips moving without sound, then looked back down with an expression that had lost every trace of nervousness.
"Two hundred and forty-two days, fourteen hours, and..." She glanced at the sun again. "Roughly twenty minutes, Your Majesty."
"Huh?" Myrasyn's ears twitched.
The precision wasn't what she'd expected from a trembling young maid, and the warmth behind it even less so. "You know the exact hour?"
"It's very important to me..." Eira whispered softly.
"I see..." Myrasyn had a tender smile of her own. "How did you come to be in his service?" Myrasyn tilted her head to study the girl's face, eager to hear the answer.
Eira's hands faltered, and her eyes darted toward Jasmine three chairs over. The governor met her gaze and gave her a small nod, her smile warm and encouraging.

"Lady Amara and Lady Vivienne Greenvale..." Eira whispered, voice turning tense. "The Greenvale Duke's daughters purchased me to be their plaything. Master Quinlan attacked them on their way back from the slave auction and freed me."
Hearing those words, Alexios's expression had gone weary.

sentences.text: The [Warp Gate] had deposited them on a snow-covered hill a few hundred meters from New Whisperfield's northern edge, and Myrasyn was squinting before anyone else had even stepped through.
"Isveth." She grabbed the other elf's arm without looking away from the view.
"Are those trees inside the city?"
Isveth's eyes narrowed against the winter glare.

A settlement of compressed earth buildings stretched across several square kilometers of forest below them, three stories tall with frosted quartz windows and external stone staircases, its roads woven between old-growth oaks and evergreen groves that stood inside the city as though the builders had refused to cut a single one.
"They built around them..." Isveth confirmed, and her grip on her own wrist tightened.
"As expected of the Holy Son..."
"And the streets are not snowy at all!" Myrasyn squinted, shading her eyes with one hand.
"Are those...
Children?" Isveth said.
"Running merrily in the cold winter?"
The rest of the procession filed through behind them.
Alexios emerged with Felicity at his side, and the warrior king's stride slowed as his gaze swept the city.
"The bastard really has a city..."
"When will you call Quinlan by his name?" Felicity giggled.
"When he stops being a bastard."
Elisabeth stepped through next and whatever complaint had been building behind her teeth dissolved into stunned silence.
"What is that?!" she shouted, pointing at the settlement in the distance.
Morgana came next, still caked in mud from her underground imprisonment.
The procession finished by Quinlan and Jasmine, walking hand-in-hand.
The guests might have stood there squinting at the settlement for another hour, but movement along the treeline cut the awe short.
A patrol of soldiers crested the hill from the east in tight formation, weapons drawn, their boots crunching through the snow with a discipline that spoke to orders taken seriously.
They'd registered the new arrivals and closed the distance fast.
This hill was priority target to defend, as enemies could use it to barrage New Whisperfield with cannon fire should it be taken.
As such, patrols were a constant in the area.
"Hands in the air and identify yourselves or we will-!" the commander shouted, but then spotted Jasmine first and faltered.
Then he spotted the man beside her.
"My Lord?!
Governor?!"
Jasmine waved them off.
"Stand down, captain.
They're our guests."
"Yes!" Fists snapped to chests in salute toward their governor.
The patrol leader's eyes lingered on Quinlan for one more heartbeat before training won out over curiosity, and the soldiers resumed their route without another word.
Jasmine turned back to her guests with a sly smile.
"If we want an authentic experience, we'll need to blend in."

Her gaze then drifted upward to the two-meter-tall armored figure beside her whose silhouette could probably be identified from a kilometer away by anyone on the continent who had ever heard the words 'Primordial Villain.'
She giggled softly.
"Well... as much as possible."
"Synchra, let's try our best, shall we?" Quinlan replied, addressing his armor.
Synchra's plates shivered with delight at the task, and the living metal began reshaping with the fussy enthusiasm of a woman who'd just been asked to dress her man for an outing.
Her first attempt was a merchant's traveling coat, deep green with brass buttons and a collar that framed his face rather well.
She held the look for a moment, pleased with herself, but then adjusted the collar, adjusted it again, and apparently decided it was too handsome.
The plates rippled into a second try, becoming a farmer's vest over roughspun, worn belt, rolled sleeves, but she fussed with the hem for two full seconds before scrapping that one too.
The third time, she committed.
Obsidian darkened to rough-spun brown, angular segments softened into the loose folds of a laborer's tunic, greaves melted into cracked leather boots.
She added stains, frayed edges, and a patch on the left knee that looked like it had been there for years.
The outfit looked like it hadn't been washed in a week, and Synchra rippled once with quiet satisfaction, finally content with what she'd made for him.
"Good job."
Quinlan's grin was entirely too pleased for the filthy garb she'd dressed him in.
The guests stared.
Not just at the transformation itself, though the fact that an armor could reshape on command was worth several questions from any smith alive.
What arrested them was that the Primordial Villain, the most dangerous man on the continent, had just voluntarily dressed himself as a pauper.
In a world where a man's station was his armor and no noble would be caught dead in commoner cloth, Quinlan wore it without complaint.

"..." Alexios then looked down at his own golden plate, at the royal crest of Vraven stamped into the breastplate, at armor that was very much incapable of turning into anything other than what it was.
"My armor can't do that.
You expect me to strip bare or what?"

Quinlan wasted no time, offering an offhanded command while adjusting his garbs: "I know we're enemies, you exhibitionist freak, but I'd appreciate it if you attacked me with honor and not war crimes."
Quinlan flicked two fingers and a second [Warp Gate] bloomed open behind him.
Emily came through first.
The head maid emerged with her hands clasped at her waist, posture straight, hair pinned, apron pressed.
Behind her came Clarisse, dignified and unhurried, then the twins Anna and Beatrice in step, then Dorothy, Eira, Ilde, and Cecile in a line so neat it could have been rehearsed.
Eight women in pressed uniforms, each carrying a leather case or folded bundle under her arm.
These were ordinary women, some young and some weathered, with calloused fingers and builds shaped by hard lives rather than noble schools.

But the precision of their formation, the quiet coordination in how they moved, and the way every one of them stood a little taller upon arriving before their master told a different story than their faces did.
"Master." Emily dipped her head toward Quinlan, then swept her eyes across the assembled royals without so much as a blink.
"Congratulations on your victory."
"Much appreciated.
Has everything been prepared?"
"Yes, we're ready."
"Capable as always, hmm?" Quinlan's voice carried a warmth the guests hadn't heard from him all day.
"We strive to please!" Emily beamed, and so did the others behind her hearing his praise.
He looked across the eight women, fond and genuine, then turned to the assembled kings and queens.
"Aren't my maids amazing?
They worked incredibly hard to become as skilled as they are."
His expression shifted, looking at his guests.
"Any insult thrown at them is the equivalent of declaring war on me, got it?" His tone was playful, jestful, yet Anna and Beatrice went scarlet in unison.
Eira ducked her head.
Cecile bit her lip and couldn't suppress the smile.
The maids, with some struggle to retain their professionalism, moved.
Chairs were brought out, lightweight and collapsible.
They set them in a half-circle facing the settlement, so the guests could watch the winter city while the work was done.
Brushes, pins, powders, ties, and clothing bundles emerged from the remaining cases with the organized efficiency of kits that had been packed and maintained well before this morning.
"Please sit," Emily asked.
Alexios dropped into his chair first, crossed his legs, and watched the proceedings with mild amusement, too old and too seasoned to find any of this beneath him.
The maid assigned to him, Ilde, began working on his armor straps, and the King of Vraven offered her the same cooperation he would have offered a field medic removing his plate after battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 1772 Misbehaving Boys
paragraphs: "Ohh..." Myrasyn was quiet for a moment.
Then understanding settled over her features, gentle and unhurried, because of course a girl who had been saved from that would know the exact hour it happened.
"I see," she said. "I'm glad you found your home."
Eira's composure held for exactly one more breath before her eyes went glassy, and she returned to the braids with hands that trembled for an entirely different reason than before.
"Thank you..."
Myrasyn's ears twitched upward, and the smile that crossed her face had sharpened into curiosity.
She leaned toward Isveth, who sat beside her with Beatrice managing her hair, and the two elves settled in.
"Tell us about life here," Myrasyn chirped, crossing one leg over the other. "What does your master feed you? Where do you sleep?"
"How does he treat his people?" Isveth added from beside her, and the quiet intensity behind the question said she'd been waiting to ask it since stepping through the gate.
"We want to hear everything," Myrasyn's eyes sparkled.
Eira glanced at Emily, received a subtle nod, and the shyness fell away faster than the braids she was undoing, and the choir of endless praise began flowing from the maid's lips.

A few chairs over, Felicity was bouncing in her seat while Clarisse worked on her purple hair with hands steady enough to manage both excitable princesses and squirming toddlers without breaking rhythm.
"Father, this kind lady is Clarisse!" Felicity announced, waving toward the eldest maid. "She's the only proper career maid in the whole household! All the others were trained by her!"
Alexios glanced at the woman, observed for a long second, then... "A fine young lady," he remarked.
Clarisse's eyes narrowed just enough to make her position clear. "His Majesty seems to be enjoying his time away from the palace."
Alexios quickly caught himself. "My apologies. Must be the adrenaline."
Clarisse offered a small curtsy toward the king, accepting the apology.
"Finally looking for a new wife, old man?" Quinlan called over without looking up. "Good on you, but stop chatting up my maids. They deserve better."
Two glares hit him from opposite directions.
Morgana's came from beneath a mask of mud and wounded fury, because she was standing right there.
Clarisse's was quieter, but no less lethal, the career maid turning her narrowed eyes on her own master.

"Master Quinlan." Clarisse's tone could have frozen the heated streets below. "I'm happy to see that you found a male friend after all these months of being surrounded exclusively by women, but I'd hope you will continue behaving as a proper adult I can be proud to serve."
Quinlan raised both hands. "My apologies. Must be the adrenaline."
"Master Quinlan..." Clarisse didn't seem entertained.
And just like that, the two most powerful men on the continent exchanged a glance after being scolded like misbehaving boys by their strict mother.
At the end of the line, Cecile approached Morgana with a brush and a fresh set of commoner clothes.
The Queen of Vraven sat in her chair like a woman who had been buried alive, dragged out of the earth, ignored by her husband, and was now being asked to cooperate with a teenager holding a brush.
Because that was exactly what had happened.
Cecile studied Morgana's mud-caked face, her filth-matted hair, her gown that looked like it had been pulled through a quarry, and tilted her head.
"Actually, your makeup is already perfect!"
Morgana's left eye twitched. "I beg your pardon?"
"You're ready to go as is!" Cecile chirped.
Morgana couldn't believe her ears. "You will clean me properly, maid."

"Nope~ My duty today is to help everyone blend in with the common folk," Cecile explained cheerfully, gesturing at the settlement below. "And you already look like you've been working in the fields all day! You're perfect as you are! If anyone asks, tell them you slipped and fell face first into the mud and no one will question your cover!"
"Clean. Me."
Cecile shook her head with genuine sympathy. "I'm sorry, but my orders are to help you blend in, not make you pretty. You blend in beautifully!"
"I AM COVERED IN DIRT!"
"Exactly!"

Morgana's hands gripped the arms of the chair hard enough to crack the wood, and the eruption building in her lungs was probably audible from the settlement when Jasmine's voice cut across from two seats over.
"Behave, Your Majesty." The Tyrant of Commerce didn't look up from the clipboard she'd produced. "Or I'll have you whipped."
The Queen of Vraven turned her blazing gaze on the brunette who had just given her an order. A lowborn merchant girl. Telling a queen. To behave. Or else.
Morgana's fury short-circuited into speechless offense.
Jasmine continued writing.
Beside Dorothy, Elisabeth had been watching her assigned maid work with genuine appreciation.
"You're very skilled," she said, and the warmth in her voice carried none of the venom she reserved for the maid's master. "Your hands are steady."
"Thank you, Your Holiness." Dorothy smiled. "We practice every day."
"May I ask something? Has he..." Elisabeth chose the word carefully. "Enslaved you?"
Dorothy's face lit up like a lantern.
"Yes!"
The word came out so bright, so proud, so thoroughly delighted that Elisabeth physically leaned back in her chair.
"W-what do you mean? Why are you happy?"
"It's the greatest honor," Dorothy continued, pressing both hands together. "Being one of Master's slaves means he trusts you completely!"
Elisabeth's mouth opened. Closed. Opened again.
"Being his slave... is a sign of his trust?"
"Yes!!" Dorothy beamed, and there was nothing in her voice but absolute, unblemished sincerity.
Elisabeth turned to look at Quinlan.
She didn't understand.

These women weren't just happy to have respectable work. Being a maid in a lord's household was already a boon for lowborn women, a giant step up from the fields and the slums, and gratitude alone could explain steady hands and polished manners.
But that wasn't what Elisabeth was seeing.
Every few seconds, one of them would steal a glance at Quinlan.
Each look lingered too long to be professional, a woman soaking in his presence while she had the chance, as if being near him was the reward and the work was just the excuse.

Eira's eyes kept drifting toward him between braids. Dorothy smiled to herself while adjusting a buckle, and the smile had nothing to do with the buckle. Even Clarisse, the one who carried herself like she answered to no one, stood a little differently when he spoke up.
They weren't mere hired servants.
Elisabeth could hear it in the way they talked about him, not "the lord" or "our employer" but "Master," spoken with the same reverence her priestesses used for the Goddess.
These women shared a history with Quinlan that went deeper than employment, deeper than loyalty, and she could not make it fit inside her head.
Then, after a few minutes of the maids working diligently, Jasmine clapped her hands and rose from her chair. "Time to move."
The maids finished their last adjustments with practiced speed.

Cloaks and robes materialized from the remaining bundles, plain wool and roughspun in muted browns and greys, draped over golden armor and royal gowns until every king, queen, and priestess on the hill looked like a group of travelers who had seen better decades.
Myrasyn ran her fingers along the coarse fabric of her cloak and smiled as though she'd been handed a new toy, but before she could pull the hood up, Quinlan stepped in front of her.
"May I?"
Myrasyn blinked, the four-thousand-year-old queen suddenly unsure what she'd just been asked, but she nodded. "Y-yes?"
Quinlan's fingers reached for her ears.
Long, elegant, unmistakably elven ears that would give her away the moment anyone on the street got a proper look.
He gathered her hair around them with practiced ease, tucking the pointed tips beneath blonde strands until they disappeared, then adjusted a few loose sections to keep them covered.
"I've done this for Seraphiel a few times," he explained casually, smoothing a strand into place. "Though she usually just pretended to be my elven sex slave. Made disguises a lot simpler."
Myrasyn's face went crimson from her collarbones to the tips of the ears he was currently hiding. "I... see..."
"There." He pulled the hood up over her hair and stepped back. "Should hold, hopefully."
Myrasyn nodded quickly, not trusting her voice, and busied herself adjusting her cloak while her ears burned beneath it.
A few steps away, Isveth had already pulled her hood up and tucked her own ears with practiced efficiency.
She stood like that for about three seconds.
Then she reached up, pulled the hood back down, and carefully untucked both ears, letting them spring free.

She turned toward Quinlan, hands clasped in front of her, and trembling desperation warped her expression, her dignity as head shrine maiden at war with the fact that the Holy Son's fingers had just been in another elf's hair and not hers.
"H-Holy Son..."
She didn't finish the sentence. She didn't dare to.
Quinlan glanced at her, then shook his head with a grin he couldn't fight down. "Come here."
Isveth crossed the distance so fast her composure didn't survive the first step.

She planted herself in front of him and tilted her head, offering both ears with her eyes squeezed shut and her clasped hands shaking, as if the Holy Son tucking her ears beneath her hair was a sacred rite she had been waiting her entire life to receive.
Quinlan tucked them in the same way he'd done for Myrasyn, and Isveth trembled through every second of it.
"There you go," he said, pulling her hood up. "Let me know if you feel it coming loose."
Isveth didn't move.
"Thank you..." Eyes still closed, fingers still clasped, the bliss radiating from her so thick it was almost visible.
"...You can open your eyes."
"Yes..." she did so, and big, happy tears rushed down her cheeks.
"Come on... Must you shrine maidens always be so dramatic?" Quinlan sighed, reaching up to clean her eyes with a finger.
Isveth nearly died on the spot.
And just like that, it was time to showcase what living under Quinlan's rule looked like!

chapters.title: Chapter 1773 Into New Whisperfield
paragraphs: The city announced itself before they reached its edge.

Sound came to greet them, hammering and voices and a child's laugh carrying over the wind, and then warmth crept through the soles of their boots twenty steps from the nearest building as the snow underfoot thinned to slush, then bare earth, then dry stone.
"Defenses... Yeah, we're working on it," Jasmine chuckled dryly under her breath, noting how the soldiers didn't give them much trouble.
In fact, they just strolled right in.
But to their credit, at least the outside patrols caught them.
"Heads gonna roll?" Felicity giggled.
"No... Not yet. They're only settling in."
"Settling in?" Myrasyn asked, confused. "Your guards are?"
"Something like that~" None who were in the know explained, instead wearing sly grins.
The reveal would have to wait.
"Hmm... What nasty young ladies you are... Tormenting your elders with suspense..." The elven queen narrowed her eyes, pouting, then began diligently studying her surroundings to unearth the mystery.

While that would take some time, what was instantly apparent to her was how every step was warmer than the last, and by the time Jasmine led them past the first row of buildings, the winter they'd left on the hilltop felt like a different country.

Heated stone stretched in every direction, dry and clean despite the winter pressing in from the treeline, and the buildings lining the main road rose three stories of compressed earth with frosted quartz windows that caught the pale light in amber.
Between them stood oaks and evergreens the builders had refused to touch, their branches heavy with snow while the roads beneath stayed bare.
"Approve... So pretty... Amazing..." Isveth nodded to herself every few seconds, seeing a new tree or other greenery show up, as if she was grading the Holy Son's city.

Kids were kicking a leather ball between stacked crates, barefoot on the warm ground, and the screaming that accompanied the game had the sort of unhinged enthusiasm that could only come from having been at it for hours.
A woman leaning out of a second-story window was mid-conversation with her neighbor below.

"You can't even compare! Back home I couldn't afford firewood half the winter, and here in New Whisperfield the ground heats itself!" She laughed, bright and disbelieving. "We haven't even finished unpacking but I love it so much better already!"
Alexios's stride slowed. "New Whisperfield?"
That... Whisperfield...?
The one that was his settlement in Ravenshade?!
The border county's capital?!
"I might've relocated your city's one hundred thousand citizens." Quinlan shrugged with not an atom of regret existing in his entire being. "Oops."
"You did what?" Alexios couldn't believe his ears.
"Whisperfield was taken a little more than a day ago!" Myrasyn yelped quietly from beneath her hood. Then her eyes widened and her head whipped toward Jasmine.
"Is that why the guards are still 'settling in?!'"
"Bingo~ They're hard-working people. Just need to give them some time."
Quinlan added nothing of his own, letting his proud governor do the talking since she seemed to be really in her element.
Far be it from Quinlan to interrupt when one of his girls was this chirpy and cheery, electing to just listen to her go on with a content heart.
Then a burst of laughter drew every eye to a small square where two roads met.
A boy of seven or eight stood on an overturned crate with his arms raised, palms pushing toward the sky.
"BRRRMMMM!" he bellowed, cheeks puffed with effort. "The cool guy with the pretty brown-haired lady did it like this! And the buildings rose!"
A smaller girl beside him was rising from a crouch with her arms stiff at her sides, being the building.
Then she began complaining, dissatisfied. "I want to be the pretty lady, not the buildings!"
"We don't have enough of us for that!"
"..." the little girl began pouting hard, reminding the onlookers of a certain overly expressive elven queen.
A third kid smacked the first one's shoulder. "No, the stairs came after! They grew out of the wall like..." He spiraled a finger upward. "Tktktktkt!" The boy on the crate pushed harder.
"Nuh-uh! He did it all at once! BRRMMM, BRRMMM!" The building-girl toppled over and started giggling, forgetting she was busy complaining.
Quinlan watched them with his hands in his pockets, grinning inwardly.
"You did the finishing touches while they were watching?" Alexios shook his head. "You truly can't help yourself but show off, can you?"

"Finishing touches?" Quinlan looked at the old man with innocence that looked so wrong on his face that Alexios shivered from head to toe and reached for the hilt of his blade, prompting Quinlan's eyes to dance with amusement as he explained, "I built it from scratch while they watched. Threw it together in a couple hours."
"You did what?!" Alexios shouted, bewildered beyond belief.

"Stop screaming you senile fucker, you'll blow our cover. And yeah." Quinlan shrugged. "Only had a few hours because I had to get back to robbing your other cities blind before Elvardia could hog all the spoils."
"..." For once, Alexios didn't even have it in him to call him a bastard.
The sheer scale of what Quinlan had done here... The quality, the quantity, the speed...
Just the fact that he relocated this many people to a place that was clearly extremely far from the original Whisperfield... Located in the wilderness no less...

But no, the people who should be huddled together while freezing to death under tree branches while the men did a mad rush to put together some shabby shacks were having the time of their lives, settling in with joyous faces.
'Not just joyous... Hopeful.'
They were hopeful for their future.
The old king felt his knees shake, something he never experienced no matter what enemy stood before him.

Myrasyn's lips curved beneath her hood. "We knew you were spiriting the human citizens from under our nose but the benefits you brought to the war effort were too valuable to make a problem out of this." Her tone carried more amusement than accusation or anger. "But to think you were taking them to make them your own citizens...?"
Then her eyes caught a detail that made her stop. "I only see humans. What have you done with the non-human slaves you took?"
"We'll get to that shortly, don't you worry," Quinlan mused mysteriously.
"Hmph!" A second deadly pout materialized on the gorgeous queen's delicate lips. "So many secrets... My heart can't take this!"
"You'll manage."
"So cruel... A family of sadists!" Then she whispered under her breath, in a note that was far too low, "No wonder Black Fang likes you so much..."
"Hmm?"
"Nothing!"
"Hold on." Elisabeth pushed forward, golden hair slipping free of her hood. "Don't just brush past what he said! He built all of this in a few hours?!"

Quinlan looked around as if seeing the city for the first time and finding it somewhat lacking. "It's a bit shabby, I know. I could've done a better job if I really wanted to, but as I said, I was limited for time and I prefer giving people a skeleton and letting them make it their own instead of giving them the finished product."

"I didn't mean it like that! What you did here is..." she bit her lip, not wanting to say the next word. But there was no helping it. The priestess gulped her pride down and whispered, "Otherworldly."
"Thanks. I didn't know you could be nice."
"... I'm an Arch Priestes... Helper and protector of the people..." she might've complained, but the argument came out weak.
"Guess I'm not a person, then?"
"..." Her expression soured, much to Quinlan's internal enjoyment. He didn't show any of it, of course.
The next stretch of street proved his point of this being a skeleton ripe for customization without a word.
A man was painting his earthen wall a deep red while his daughter held the bucket. Two women argued about curtain colors for a window they hadn't installed yet.
A flower box hung from a railing that had been bare stone hours ago, bright petals against brown earth.
Morgana, who had been silent since the foot of the hill, spoke.
"The heat." The words came out like they cost her something. "How?"
"I created a magma chamber beneath the bedrock then branched its conduits into every building. The people get just enough to give them heat without turning their homes into a cooking pot."

Quinlan kept walking as he explained. "After some trial and error, I managed to create a passive system that refuels itself in said magma chamber. Well, we'll see how long that cycle lasts, but it should go for at least a few years."
To every leader in the procession, what he explained with casual nonchalance was a sign of unbelievable power.

Morgana replied with nothing, and her silence carried more weight than any of Elisabeth's outbursts, because the Queen of Vraven understood exactly how difficult carving a geothermal network through bedrock was.
'Difficult...? More like impossible. The amount of precise elemental manipulation needed, combined with the unfathomable mana expenditure that must've accompanied it...'
All of a sudden, the queen's eyes began swirling again as she couldn't help herself but want to study him all over again, her curiosity rekindled in full.
"Stop staring at my boyfriend like that, psycho," Jasmine chimed in, and Morgana's head whipped sideways as if she was slapped.
'I'll murder this haughty bitch!' she cursed inwardly, without opening her mouth. She knew better.

But that didn't stop her from complaining inwardly. 'Why are none of them standing up for me?! She threatened me with whipping and now called me a psycho, and my husband and daughters don't even react!'
Alexios was far too busy to care, as he felt his legs go weak all over again.
