chapters.title: Chapter 1781 Joining the Fun
paragraphs: "Can we join?" Quinlan asked, nonchalantly ignoring the screeching.
"...Join?"
"We're hungry."
Mira's mouth opened. Closed.

She looked at the children already swarming him, then back at him, and the sheer absurdity of the Primordial Villain asking to sit down for a picnic with her orphans rendered her completely speechless.
The elf sister and the wolfkin sister rose and bowed to Quinlan. "Sir, it would be our honor."
"Thank you," Quinlan smiled.
He produced a wide blanket from his pocket ring and spread it beside the children's.
Jasmine sat down next to him before the fabric had settled, crossed her ankles, and turned to the elf sister with the governor's smile.
"How have things been? Any issues with the last shipment?"
"Everything has been wonderful, Governor Argentis. The children have been eating well and the new building materials arrived on time."
While Jasmine talked logistics, Mira's brain was catching up with the guests stepping off the wind and settling onto the blanket, one face at a time.
The blonde in roughspun. Those golden eyes.
"...Elisabeth the Dawn Breaker?!"
The older man beside her.
Grey hair.
Regal bearing that commoner's clothes did nothing to hide.
"King Alexios?!"
The purple-haired girl who had already leapt from the blanket and was running toward the children.
"Princess Felicity?!"
Then two elven women lowered their hoods, and the ears that emerged were so long, so perfect, and so unmistakably royal that Mira's knees buckled.
"ELF QUEEN MYRASYN?!"

Hearing those words, the elf sister's composure shattered. She rose and tried to bow to Myrasyn, hands trembling. "Your Majesty, I- forgive me, I didn't recognize you... I grew up in slavery, I've never seen your portrait-"
Myrasyn took the nun's hands before she could finish.
She held them steady, met her eyes, and smiled.
"May we join you?"
The elf sister blinked. The trembling stopped. "...It would be our pleasure, Your Majesty."
"Just call me Myrasyn," the queen corrected gently. "I already surrendered my throne to the man you now follow."
"!!" All three nuns' eyes flew wide open at the casual revelation.

Isveth was already settling onto the blanket beside her queen, tucking her legs beneath her and studying the children around them with bright eyes and a smile she couldn't have suppressed if she tried.
The blankets merged.
Children rearranged themselves around the newcomers with the fearless curiosity of creatures too young to know what "continental power" meant, and Quinlan began pulling food from his pocket ring.
Roasted meats wrapped in wax paper.
Honeyed bread that steamed when unwrapped.
Pastries dusted with powdered sugar.
Fruits in colors the children had never seen.
The pile grew until the dwarven boy's eyes took up half his face.
"Did you have any cool fights?!" a human boy asked, bouncing on his knees.
"Just came from a big one," Quinlan said, tearing a piece of bread.
"Did you win?!"
"Obviously."
"Did you punch anyone?!"
"Not even his mother could recognize him now."
"COOL!!"
The elf girl edged closer. "Were you hurt?" she asked, and the care in her voice was buried so deep beneath composure that only a fellow elf would have caught it.
"Yes, but my pretty elf wife patched me up really well."
"Hmph!! ...Good." She looked away, cheeks puffed. "Not that I was concerned."
The mood settled in the next few minutes.
Chewing replaced shouting.
Circles formed as naturally as water finding its level, children drifting toward whichever adult they were curious about.
A human boy of six walked up to Isveth, dropped to one knee, and placed his hand over his heart.

"Beautiful lady," he announced, projecting his voice so the entire clearing could hear, "your eyes are strong like a warrior's but your face is gentle like a princess. Your ears are long and elegant and I think they're really cute." He drew a breath. "I have decided that I will marry you when I grow up. Please wait for me!"
Isveth's mouth fell open. "Huh?"
Before she could respond, a human girl the same age marched over and smacked him on the back of the head.
"You said the SAME THING to ME yesterday!"
"That's not true! I said your eyes were pretty, not strong! And your ears are much shorter! It's completely different!"
The girl smacked him again.
The boy fled.
Isveth covered her mouth with both hands, doing her best to remain graceful, yet... "Hahaha!" adoring laughter pushed through.
Felicity had gathered the older girls around her within minutes, and they were deep in whispered conference, shooting glances at the boys and collapsing into giggles behind cupped hands.
She fit among them so naturally that Alexios had to look twice to find her.
A tigerkin girl, barely four, wandered away from the group and climbed into Myrasyn's lap without asking.
She settled there as if it were the most natural seat in the clearing, then craned her neck far enough to look up.
"Your ears are really long," she said. "Can you hear really far?"
Myrasyn's hands hovered, not knowing where to rest. "Yes, but one day you might give me a run for my money, young lady..."
"I will. But..." The girl leaned back against the queen's chest and patted her hand twice. "Headpats please."
"Kyaa!!" Myrasyn squealed as her fingers settled on the girl's head, and she began stroking her hair with careful, trembling fingers.
Morgana stood with her back against a tree, arms crossed, turned away from the blankets and everyone on them. Dirt still caked her face.
Her commands forbade her from washing it off.
A small girl wandered over and tilted her head. "Your face is dirty."
She produced a wrinkled cloth from her pocket and rose on tiptoe, holding it up. She waited.
"Can I help?"
Morgana looked at the cloth. Looked at the child.
Nothing in her commands said she couldn't let someone else do it.
Then she bent her head forward.
The girl wiped mud from the Queen of Vraven's cheek with small, careful strokes, tongue poking out in concentration. When she finished, she stepped back and studied her work. "Better!"
Morgana straightened.
She looked entirely lost on what to do.
Gratitude wasn't her strongest of suits.

Then, her fingers moved through three precise gestures, lips forming words that hummed with old resonance, and ice gathered between her palms, violet and warm, spinning into a crystalline flower that caught the winter sun and threw tiny prisms across the girl's face.
She pressed it into the child's hands.
"Here. Now go."
The girl's eyes lit up. "Thank you, pretty lady!"
Felicity watched from across the blanket, and the smile on her face was the proudest she'd worn all day.
Quinlan caught Morgana's eye, amused.
"Stop staring," she hissed, and looked away.
A dwarven boy tugged at Elisabeth's sleeve. "Hey. You're wearing a Goddess thing." He pointed at the sigil.
"I am the Arch Priestess of-"
"Can you bless our food? Sister Mira does it every day but she says hers probably aren't as good as a real one."
Elisabeth looked at the blankets spread before her.

Elven children beside dwarven children beside beastkin children beside human children, crumbs on every face, milk on every chin, a beastkin girl getting headpats in the Queen of Elvardia's lap while a crystalline flower glittered in another child's hands.
She clasped her hands and bowed her head.

"Goddess who watches over all," she began, and her voice held steady, "bless this meal and those who share it. Bless the hands that prepared it, bless the children who eat it, and bless the ground beneath them that keeps them warm and safe." Her breath hitched. "No matter where they came from... may they never go hungry again."
When she finished, the dwarven boy nodded. "Thanks." He went back to eating.
Elisabeth sat very still. "This... Am I dreaming?" Then she wiped her eyes with the back of her hand and blamed the wind.
Alexios sat at the edge of the blanket with his elbows on his knees.
A boy brought him a piece of honeyed bread, not because he recognized the king, but because the old man sitting alone looked like he could use one.
"Here, gramps."
Alexios took it. "Much appreciated."
The boy ran back to his friends.
These were children of his kingdom.
Freed from being slaves, or orphaned under his rule, during wars he'd presided over, slave hunts his ancestors endorsed and he didn't demolish, in a world he'd shaped for a thousand years.

They were here now because a man he'd called villain had built them a home where an elf could argue with a dwarf about what counted as food and a wolfkin could pour milk for everyone and a nun in dirty robes could be the first person every child ran to.
The bread sat in his hands. He took a bite.
It was bittersweet.
They entered Miri Town through its southern gate, and the settlement swallowed them whole.

chapters.title: Chapter 1782 Absolute Tyranny
paragraphs: They entered Miri Town through its southern gate, and the settlement swallowed them whole.
Where New Whisperfield had been a human city with human rhythms, Miri Town hit the senses from every direction at once.
A dwarven smith's forge sat beside an elven herbalist's shop, the clang of hammer on steel mixing with the scent of dried lavender.
Trees grew through the upper floors of buildings where no human architect would have left the gap, and staircases descended into underground passages that glowed faintly with embedded quartz.
"I can't believe my eyes..." Alexios whispered, struggling to process what he was seeing.
A dwarven woman carried crates alongside a human man, arguing about stacking order.
An elven girl sold woven bracelets from a stall while a beastkin boy swept the space beside her.
A human mother called her children in for dinner from a doorway, and two of the three kids who came running had pointed ears.
"Yes, mom!!"
As interracial breeding wasn't a thing in Thalorind, it could only mean one thing: a human decided to adopt elves.
"Is this reality? Or am I dreaming...?" Myrasyn breathed in disbelief.
Quinlan walked with his hands in his pockets, Jasmine at his side, and he let the question sit for a few steps before answering.

"Take away the politics and people just want to live. They want to eat, build a life they can be proud of, raise kids, and sleep without worrying about what's coming through the door. On a fundamental level, I believe that every race wants the same things."
"The hatred is inherited, not innate, hmm?" Alexios muttered.

"Certain races tend to have stronger friction with one another, no doubt," Quinlan mused, looking at Myrasyn who, for once, did not seem too intent on looking back at him as he added, "But no one is born with racial hatred. It comes from circumstance, from politics, from what papa and mama tells their young children. Those kids back there proved it."
He paused at a corner where a dwarven craftsman sat on a crate with his arms crossed, watching a human boy struggle with a chisel.
The boy's grip was wrong, his angle was worse, and the dwarf's expression said he'd seen better work from a blind goat.
"I don't think you can impress me," the dwarf said flatly. "But if you do, I might take you under my wing. Gotta embrace the new way of life or I'll be left behind."
The boy's jaw set. He adjusted his grip, squared his shoulders, and attacked the stone with desperate focus. "I'll prove it!"
"Hmph. We'll see about that, lad." The dwarf didn't smile, but he didn't leave either.
A few steps further, an elven woman sat on a bench beside a dogkin boy of ten, guiding his fingers through the stems of a flower wreath. The boy fumbled a petal loose.
"Gently," the elf said. "If you rush it, the stems break. This will surely impress Little Ruby if you do it right."
The boy's tail wagged once, shy and quick, and he bent back over the wreath, more careful this time.
Quinlan watched both scenes pass, then admitted:
"But I'd be lying if I told you it's that simple."
Myrasyn looked at him.

"All of this only works because I'm an absolute tyrant," Quinlan admitted without missing a beat. "I don't negotiate. I don't hold votes. I set the rules and everyone follows them, because the alternative is punishment."
"The moment you die, it all falls apart," Alexios said.
Jasmine, Felicity, Isveth, and Myrasyn turned to look at him in unison, and the combined fury in their eyes could have set the street on fire.
Alexios shrugged. "What? It's true."
Quinlan chuckled. "He's right. But I don't plan on dying, old man."
"No one does," Alexios said.
"Of course." Quinlan grinned, hands in his pockets. "Death is a real risk. But unlike others, I'm an unaging primordial. The only way I can die is by being killed."
A strong glint sharpened behind his eyes, ominous. "And after Ragnar so kindly gave me a wake up call, I've been taking strong measures to avoid just that."
The group went quiet.

The street opened into a small square where a former slave, an elven woman with faded scars on her throat, was arguing with her human neighbor about a fence that leaned two inches into her yard. The argument was loud, petty, and completely mundane.
Alexios watched them, and the realization settled into place instantly.
It wasn't just the tyranny. Any ruler with enough power could be a tyrant.
It wasn't just his power either. While anomalous and overwhelming, that wouldn't be enough on its own.
Instead, the real difference maker was that Quinlan had no side.
He looked human but he wasn't, and that single fact changed everything.

If Alexios tried this, his human subjects would call it betrayal the moment he favored an elf over one of their own. If Myrasyn tried it, her elves would fracture before the first dwarven family unpacked their belongings. At the same time, subjects of other races would be resisting their rule with every fiber of their being, aware that their racial disposition makes them naturally favor their own people over them.
Every ruler on the continent carried their race like a chain around their neck, and every decision they made was weighed against it.
Quinlan carried nothing.
He was the only person alive who could sit between every race and be trusted by all of them, because he belonged to none of them.
Absolute tyranny was the method.
Immense power and wealth were the tools.
True, one-of-a-kind racial neutrality was the miracle.
"...What about funding?" Alexios grunted. Such an undertaking required immense starting capital.

"I've been robbing your cities blind for a reason." The casual tone returned to Quinlan as if the most honest political statement of the century had been a passing thought. "But I'm always open for charitable donations."
"..." Alexios's fists clenched.

"That said, if you want me to feel even slightly moved by the gesture you should hurry up, old friend..." Quinlan mused, voice proud. "After all, soon..." He gestured at the square and let it speak for itself.
Alexios's eyes followed the gesture, and he didn't need to be lectured for the economics to click.

Dwarven craftsmen who would have spent their lives forging the same regulation blades in the same regulation foundries were here, free to innovate, teaching human apprentices techniques no human smith had ever seen.

Elven artisans who only traded among themselves due to politics, and even that at a low volume, were now selling handmade wares at stalls, their finishing work so precise it turned basic tools into luxury goods.
Beastkin with stamina no laborer could match were hauling supply crates up streets that would have broken a human crew's backs by noon.
Every race brought something the others lacked, and someone had put them all in one place and told them to get along.
The economic potential was staggering.
And it had been built with his stolen treasury.
And the arrogant fucker dared to say he's open to more donations.
And that he should hurry up if he wanted it to mean something?!?!
Jasmine confirmed what the king's eyes already told him. "The first exports left Miri Town only a few days ago, actually. We smuggled them into Greenvale cities using my connections."
She grinned, openly proud at the achievement of their subjects like her lover. "The margins were absurd."
They walked deeper.
An underground entrance gaped beside a staircase that spiraled up into the canopy, the two paths diverging from the same street corner.
A dwarf went down. An elf went up. A human woman went straight.

"The infrastructure adapts to whoever lives in it," Jasmine explained, reading the guests' faces. "Dwarves get underground workshops and living quarters. Elves get canopy walkways and gardens. Beastkin get open training grounds. Humans get the standard layout they're used to. Well, it's not that we prohibit others from living elsewhere."
"And the former slaves?" Elisabeth asked. Her voice was careful. "How can an elf abused by humans for generations of owners be expected to integrate properly?"

"They aren't expected to do anything," Jasmine replied. "First, not many slave owners are present in Miri Town. The only ones here are those who were spoken for by their own former slaves. Those who weren't spoken for but were deemed to not have abused their powers in an unforgivable way were relocated to New Whisperfield, a few of them awaiting trial. And those who were deemed to have been overly cruel and abusive were sentenced to death or enslaved and given to the slaves they abused to do with as they please."
"...An absolute tyrant..." Elisabeth mulled on those words as Jasmine added,

"Second, nobody is forced to mingle with another race. If they don't want to, they don't need to be neighbors with one another. An abused sex slave can live in her own little group until she feels ready to move on. We'll provide the best support for them to do so, but we refuse to force the issue. We just expect them to behave, and believe the rest will come with time."
The group walked in silence for a while after that, and the city spoke for itself.
Then Quinlan clapped his hands.

"I hope you enjoyed this little tour," he mused, turning to face his guests with a grin that signaled the sightseeing was over. "But I'm afraid it's time for us to move on. While a ferociously pouting Black Fang glaring at me cutely because I took too long to return home is an extremely inviting image I long to see with all my being, I fear she might elect to react rather differently."
"..." No one had a response to that.
He flicked two fingers.
Space tore open, and the shimmering surface of a [Warp Gate] bloomed in the middle of the street.
It was time to welcome his guests in his home and unearth the great mysteries of the Iskaris continent.

sentences.text: They entered Miri Town through its southern gate, and the settlement swallowed them whole.
Where New Whisperfield had been a human city with human rhythms, Miri Town hit the senses from every direction at once.
A dwarven smith's forge sat beside an elven herbalist's shop, the clang of hammer on steel mixing with the scent of dried lavender.
Trees grew through the upper floors of buildings where no human architect would have left the gap, and staircases descended into underground passages that glowed faintly with embedded quartz.
"I can't believe my eyes..." Alexios whispered, struggling to process what he was seeing.
A dwarven woman carried crates alongside a human man, arguing about stacking order.
An elven girl sold woven bracelets from a stall while a beastkin boy swept the space beside her.
A human mother called her children in for dinner from a doorway, and two of the three kids who came running had pointed ears.
"Yes, mom!!"
As interracial breeding wasn't a thing in Thalorind, it could only mean one thing: a human decided to adopt elves.
"Is this reality?
Or am I dreaming...?" Myrasyn breathed in disbelief.
Quinlan walked with his hands in his pockets, Jasmine at his side, and he let the question sit for a few steps before answering.
"Take away the politics and people just want to live.
They want to eat, build a life they can be proud of, raise kids, and sleep without worrying about what's coming through the door.
On a fundamental level, I believe that every race wants the same things."
"The hatred is inherited, not innate, hmm?" Alexios muttered.

"Certain races tend to have stronger friction with one another, no doubt," Quinlan mused, looking at Myrasyn who, for once, did not seem too intent on looking back at him as he added, "But no one is born with racial hatred.
It comes from circumstance, from politics, from what papa and mama tells their young children.
Those kids back there proved it."
He paused at a corner where a dwarven craftsman sat on a crate with his arms crossed, watching a human boy struggle with a chisel.
The boy's grip was wrong, his angle was worse, and the dwarf's expression said he'd seen better work from a blind goat.
"I don't think you can impress me," the dwarf said flatly.
"But if you do, I might take you under my wing.
Gotta embrace the new way of life or I'll be left behind."
The boy's jaw set.
He adjusted his grip, squared his shoulders, and attacked the stone with desperate focus.
"I'll prove it!"
"Hmph.
We'll see about that, lad." The dwarf didn't smile, but he didn't leave either.
A few steps further, an elven woman sat on a bench beside a dogkin boy of ten, guiding his fingers through the stems of a flower wreath.
The boy fumbled a petal loose.
"Gently," the elf said.
"If you rush it, the stems break.
This will surely impress Little Ruby if you do it right."
The boy's tail wagged once, shy and quick, and he bent back over the wreath, more careful this time.
Quinlan watched both scenes pass, then admitted:
"But I'd be lying if I told you it's that simple."
Myrasyn looked at him.
"All of this only works because I'm an absolute tyrant," Quinlan admitted without missing a beat.
"I don't negotiate.
I don't hold votes.
I set the rules and everyone follows them, because the alternative is punishment."
"The moment you die, it all falls apart," Alexios said.
Jasmine, Felicity, Isveth, and Myrasyn turned to look at him in unison, and the combined fury in their eyes could have set the street on fire.
Alexios shrugged.
"What?
It's true."
Quinlan chuckled.
"He's right.
But I don't plan on dying, old man."
"No one does," Alexios said.
"Of course." Quinlan grinned, hands in his pockets.
"Death is a real risk.
But unlike others, I'm an unaging primordial.
The only way I can die is by being killed."
A strong glint sharpened behind his eyes, ominous.
"And after Ragnar so kindly gave me a wake up call, I've been taking strong measures to avoid just that."
The group went quiet.
The street opened into a small square where a former slave, an elven woman with faded scars on her throat, was arguing with her human neighbor about a fence that leaned two inches into her yard.
The argument was loud, petty, and completely mundane.
Alexios watched them, and the realization settled into place instantly.
It wasn't just the tyranny.
Any ruler with enough power could be a tyrant.
It wasn't just his power either.
While anomalous and overwhelming, that wouldn't be enough on its own.
Instead, the real difference maker was that Quinlan had no side.
He looked human but he wasn't, and that single fact changed everything.
If Alexios tried this, his human subjects would call it betrayal the moment he favored an elf over one of their own.
If Myrasyn tried it, her elves would fracture before the first dwarven family unpacked their belongings.
At the same time, subjects of other races would be resisting their rule with every fiber of their being, aware that their racial disposition makes them naturally favor their own people over them.
Every ruler on the continent carried their race like a chain around their neck, and every decision they made was weighed against it.
Quinlan carried nothing.
He was the only person alive who could sit between every race and be trusted by all of them, because he belonged to none of them.
Absolute tyranny was the method.
Immense power and wealth were the tools.
True, one-of-a-kind racial neutrality was the miracle.
"...What about funding?" Alexios grunted.
Such an undertaking required immense starting capital.
"I've been robbing your cities blind for a reason." The casual tone returned to Quinlan as if the most honest political statement of the century had been a passing thought.
"But I'm always open for charitable donations."
"..." Alexios's fists clenched.
"That said, if you want me to feel even slightly moved by the gesture you should hurry up, old friend..." Quinlan mused, voice proud.
"After all, soon..." He gestured at the square and let it speak for itself.
Alexios's eyes followed the gesture, and he didn't need to be lectured for the economics to click.

Dwarven craftsmen who would have spent their lives forging the same regulation blades in the same regulation foundries were here, free to innovate, teaching human apprentices techniques no human smith had ever seen.

Elven artisans who only traded among themselves due to politics, and even that at a low volume, were now selling handmade wares at stalls, their finishing work so precise it turned basic tools into luxury goods.
Beastkin with stamina no laborer could match were hauling supply crates up streets that would have broken a human crew's backs by noon.
Every race brought something the others lacked, and someone had put them all in one place and told them to get along.
The economic potential was staggering.
And it had been built with his stolen treasury.
And the arrogant fucker dared to say he's open to more donations.
And that he should hurry up if he wanted it to mean something?!?!
Jasmine confirmed what the king's eyes already told him.
"The first exports left Miri Town only a few days ago, actually.
We smuggled them into Greenvale cities using my connections."
She grinned, openly proud at the achievement of their subjects like her lover.
"The margins were absurd."
They walked deeper.
An underground entrance gaped beside a staircase that spiraled up into the canopy, the two paths diverging from the same street corner.
A dwarf went down.
An elf went up.
A human woman went straight.
"The infrastructure adapts to whoever lives in it," Jasmine explained, reading the guests' faces.
"Dwarves get underground workshops and living quarters.
Elves get canopy walkways and gardens.
Beastkin get open training grounds.
Humans get the standard layout they're used to.
Well, it's not that we prohibit others from living elsewhere."
"And the former slaves?" Elisabeth asked.
Her voice was careful.
"How can an elf abused by humans for generations of owners be expected to integrate properly?"
"They aren't expected to do anything," Jasmine replied.
"First, not many slave owners are present in Miri Town.
The only ones here are those who were spoken for by their own former slaves.
Those who weren't spoken for but were deemed to not have abused their powers in an unforgivable way were relocated to New Whisperfield, a few of them awaiting trial.
And those who were deemed to have been overly cruel and abusive were sentenced to death or enslaved and given to the slaves they abused to do with as they please."
"...An absolute tyrant..." Elisabeth mulled on those words as Jasmine added,
"Second, nobody is forced to mingle with another race.
If they don't want to, they don't need to be neighbors with one another.
An abused sex slave can live in her own little group until she feels ready to move on.
We'll provide the best support for them to do so, but we refuse to force the issue.
We just expect them to behave, and believe the rest will come with time."
The group walked in silence for a while after that, and the city spoke for itself.
Then Quinlan clapped his hands.
"I hope you enjoyed this little tour," he mused, turning to face his guests with a grin that signaled the sightseeing was over.
"But I'm afraid it's time for us to move on.

While a ferociously pouting Black Fang glaring at me cutely because I took too long to return home is an extremely inviting image I long to see with all my being, I fear she might elect to react rather differently."
"..." No one had a response to that.
He flicked two fingers.
Space tore open, and the shimmering surface of a [Warp Gate] bloomed in the middle of the street.
It was time to welcome his guests in his home and unearth the great mysteries of the Iskaris continent.

chapters.title: Chapter 1783 The Villain's Home
paragraphs: Quinlan's [Warp Gate] opened onto packed earth and the scent of pine, and the group stepped through into a wide courtyard framed by tall buildings and old-growth forest on every side.
He and Jasmine emerged first with the ease of people coming home, the guests following a step behind, and the gate collapsed with a soft rush of displaced air.
Their eyes turned toward the structure ahead.
A three-story, luxury mansion sat at the courtyard's center, ivy climbing one wall in a line that suggested a gardener's hand rather than neglect.
Flanking it were smaller structures: a smithy with tools racked outside its open doors, a long barracks-style residence, a bathhouse whose copper vent trailed lazy steam into the winter air.
Heated cobblestones ran between them, and the grounds were clean, lived-in, and maintained with the kind of care that only came from people who planned to stay.
Alexios scanned the compound in one slow arc, and a grunt left him, already annoyed despite having just arrived. "All this in the middle of nowhere. Someone certainly knows how to live."
"Well," Quinlan mused, "when your enemy who wields infinitely more power than you posts a bounty on your head with a royal boon as the reward, you learn to live away from his cities."
Alexios's eye twitched.
He remembered signing that decree.
The first and only time the Vraven crown had offered a royal boon for a fugitive's capture instead of gold, a personal favor from the king redeemable without condition.
It told the continent that Alexios considered this man the most dangerous threat alive.
It told the continent that Alexios considered this man the most dangerous threat alive.

And the target of that bounty had spent his fugitive months living in a mansion with heated floors and a bathhouse, deep in unmapped forest no hunter had ever trekked, funded by robbing Alexios's subjects - and the man himself - blind.
In this moment, it felt as though the bastard's entire existence was an insult to the long life the king led.
"Hie?!"
Two gasps cut his thoughts short.
They came from behind him, soft and involuntary, and when Alexios turned he found both elves frozen where they stood.

Myrasyn's ears were moving on their own. But these were not the controlled shifts he'd grown accustomed to over the tour nor the performative twitches he believed were more or less involuntary mating calls for a certain infuriating scum.
Though he had no proof.
Instead of those, these ear movements were rapid and uncontrolled, swiveling toward the space behind the group with the urgency of a compass finding north.
Her toes had curled into the earth, her fingers hung loose at her sides, and the color had left her face.
Isveth stood beside her queen with her lips parted and her eyes huge, trembling.
"Q-Quinlan..." Myrasyn's voice barely carried. "What is standing behind us?"
"Never..." Isveth's hand found her queen's arm and gripped. "In all my years, I have never sensed a presence like this. How majestic..."
Quinlan looked at the two elves, and the grin that spread across his face was the slow, satisfied kind that answered nothing.
Alexios frowned, searching for whatever had driven both elves into that state.
It didn't take him more than a single second.
Roots. Massive roots wound through the earth like frozen rivers, twisting and braiding across the ground before plunging deep.

They were too large for any tree Alexios had seen in his thousand years of living, and the bark that covered them pulsed with veins of liquid gold that traveled in slow, visible currents beneath the surface.
'What the...'
His eyes climbed.

The trunk rose from those roots like a pillar bracing the sky itself, wider at its base than the mansion's front wall, its pale silver bark threaded with the same golden veins in branching patterns that shifted as he watched.

It climbed past the mansion's third floor and kept going, past the treeline of the surrounding forest and kept going, through the canopy overhead that he had mistaken for natural woodland when they arrived and kept going, until the crown spread against the winter sky in a vast iridescent dome of crystalline leaves that shimmered green and gold in rapid, excited pulses, throwing dancing light across the entire compound like sunlight scattered through a prism.

The tree was impossibly, unnaturally tall. It dwarfed the mansion. It dwarfed the forest. It stood like a living monument that had no business existing on a continent where nothing of its kind had been seen in recorded history.
And on one of its highest branches, silhouetted against the vast, empty sky, a very small figure stood with her hands planted firmly on her hips.

"Daddy!! You're LATE!!" The voice traveled down from the heights with a clarity that defied the distance. "Rosie has been standing here for a FULL hour, waiting! What do you have to say for yourself?!"
Her chest was puffed out so far that Alexios was mildly concerned she might topple from the branch.
Myrasyn and Isveth finally braced themselves enough to turn around.
The motion was identical and simultaneous, as if someone had wound their spines with the same key. Their heads turned with mechanical stiffness, looking more like decorated golems than elves.
Their eyes found the roots first.
Then they climbed. Slowly.
Up the golden veins.
Up the silver trunk that widened past the canopy.
Past the first spreading branches where crystalline leaves began to cluster in shimmering layers of green and gold.
Higher, through the iridescent crown that caught the light in patterns no jeweler could replicate.
Higher still, to the branch at the very top, where a tiny green-skinned girl with vine-like auburn hair stood with her fists on her hips, looking extremely displeased with her father's punctuality.
Both elves blinked.
Once.
Twice.
Then their eyes rolled back and their bodies went limp.
Quinlan was already moving. He stepped between them, catching Myrasyn against his left side and Isveth against his right before either woman hit the ground.
Their eyes had gone hazy and unfocused, and both women sagged against him like sleepwalkers.
"You could have just joined us for the tour," he called up to the branch, holding both elves upright without effort.
"Hmph!" Rosie scoffed and looked away, chin lifted. "Rosie had very important business! She wanted to impress the pretty elven ladies, and this was the best way to do it!"
Against his sides, both elves shuddered.
It wasn't just the words. The words were adorable enough on their own, but combined with 'everything' else...

For elves, beings whose senses were threaded into the living world in ways no other race could comprehend, standing in the presence of a being that was so much more than the fabled Geims from legends...
It was like being submerged. The sensory load was overbearing because Rosie - and the tree, which was a part of her existence - were standing right in front of them in all their glory.
Every golden vein pulsing through the bark sang along their nerve endings.
Every crystalline leaf shimmering above pressed against their perception the way sunlight pressed against closed eyelids.
The warmth, the vitality, the ancient thrumming life of the tree and the small creature bonded to it flooded through them in waves that all their combined years of existence had never encountered.
And the creature responsible for this sensory paradise was a very small, very pouty child who was scolding her father for being late.
The overload hit from both directions at once, and neither elf had the constitution to handle the combination.
Myrasyn's head lolled against Quinlan's shoulder. Isveth's knees buckled fully, and only Quinlan's arm around her waist kept her from sliding to the ground.
Quinlan chuckled as he looked up at the perch. "Will you forgive me?"
"No!" Rosie scoffed, arms crossed, pouting up at him from the branch. "Rosie's feet hurt from standing so long!!"
She held the pose for three heartbeats, then peeked over her shoulder. "..."
"!!!" Her gaze caught his face, and she squeezed her eyes shut before whipping her head away.
A few seconds passed.
She peeked again. "..."
Longer this time.
Her lower lip pushed out, trembling between righteous fury and the overwhelming urge to abandon it.
Elisabeth pressed both hands to her sigil and felt her knees soften. "So cute..."
As the Dawn Breaker, whose job description included hunting down terrible monstrosities, the discovery of a being with unknown origins should've made her stand at attention.
Instead, she was watching a child try to stay angry at her father and failing spectacularly.
Combativeness never even crossed her mind.
Rosie peeked a third time and didn't look away.

Her resistance crumbled from the bottom up, the pout dissolving into a wobble, the wobble melting into a helpless smile, and then the smile broke into a grin so wide and so full of joy that the crystalline leaves above her erupted in a frenzy of golden light.
Rosie jumped. "Daddy!!!"
"The child!" Myrasyn's eyes flew open and she lunged forward, every trace of her daze incinerated by the sight of a small body dropping from such a brutal height.

"She'll hurt herself!!" Isveth screamed, throwing herself out of Quinlan's hold, because whatever sensory overload had put her out of commission meant absolutely nothing when a child was plummeting from the sky.
Both women were brimming with a mother's protective instinct.
But then Quinlan stepped forward. He stood beneath the tree with his hands raised and his palms open, watching the tiny green figure plummet toward him without a flicker of concern.

Rosie hit his palms with a soft thump and a burst of giggles, and Quinlan swept her into his arms and spun on his heel, lifting her high as her laughter rose through the courtyard in the bright, unrestrained way that only a child reuniting with her father could produce.
"Hehehe!! Again! Again!!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1784 Melting Elves
paragraphs: He spun her once more, faster, and Rosie's vine-hair whipped around her face as her giggles bounced off the mansion walls.
"Everything alright back home?" he asked, settling her against his chest.
Rosie didn't answer.

She pressed her cheek against his collarbone and curled there, small green hands gripping the fabric of his tunic, and the golden veins in the tree above pulsed in slow, warm waves that matched the rhythm of her breathing.
"Rosie is so happy Daddy came back home safe..." she whispered, eyes half-closed. "And that everyone survived..."
The courtyard went quiet.
Myrasyn's vision blurred.
Beside her, Isveth's hand flew to her mouth.
Quinlan held her for a moment longer, chin resting against the top of her head. Then the warmth in his expression shifted.
A grin crept across his face, beyond mischievous, and his eyes flicked toward the two weeping elves.
"Rosie."
"Hm?"
"I brought you fresh meat."

Rosie's head came up from his chest, and the smile that split her face was her father's own, the same angle, the same width, the same scheming delight that promised trouble for everyone in the vicinity.
She wriggled free, dropped to the ground, and planted herself before Myrasyn and Isveth with her feet apart, her chest puffed, and her chin held high.
The two elves looked down.
She was very, very small.

"My name is Rosie Elysiar!!" she declared, her tiny voice carrying far more authority than her height had any right to produce. "First born daughter of Quinlan Elysiar and granddaughter of Grandmommy Luminara!!"
Both elves stopped breathing.

"And by Rosie's sacred right as the First Elf's granddaughter..." Her amber eyes sparkled as she drew herself to her full and entirely unimpressive height. "Rosie decrees that BOTH pretty elven ladies MUST pamper her like there's no tomorrow!!"
She spread her arms wide, expectant, ready to be embraced.
Myrasyn's lips moved without sound.
Isveth's tears were still falling, but her eyes had gone so wide they looked ready to leave her face.
They stared at the child.
Then at each other.
Then back at the child.
Neither moved.
Rosie's confident expression held for a few seconds before it began to falter.
She glanced toward Quinlan, and the scheme drained from her face as the two women simply stood there.
Quinlan's grin also vanished. What replaced it was so profoundly, devastatingly sad that Jasmine had to press her lips together to keep from laughing.
"You two don't want to...?" he asked, voice heavy.
Rosie looked up at the two elven women, and her eyes went round, wet, and devastatingly large. Her lower lip pushed out.
"Is Rosie too ugly for the pretty elven ladies to touch...?"
Myrasyn and Isveth's heads whipped toward Quinlan.
The devastation was already gone.
What had replaced it was so wide and so shameless it could have lit the courtyard on its own, and the look in his eyes said one thing.
"What are you waiting for?" he asked.
Myrasyn moved first.

The four-thousand-year-old queen dropped to the earth without a single thought for her attire or pristine skin, her knees hitting the ground, and her arms closed around the child before Rosie finished blinking.
"Too ugly?!" Her voice cracked on the first syllable. "Never say such a thing! It was just... You're too mesmerizing! I don't deserve this honor!"

She looked up at Quinlan from the tangle of limbs and tears and elven robes.
Quinlan gave her a thumbs up.

All sins were forgiven.

Namely, pulling the girl even tighter against her chest, stroking her vine-hair with trembling fingers as tears streamed freely down her face, and the sounds that left her were the soft, half-melodic hums that elven mothers used to soothe their young, pulled from somewhere so deep in her chest she hadn't known it was still there.
"This is the best day of my life..." she whimpered.

Isveth pressed her forehead against Rosie's small shoulder, tears refusing to stop flowing, and her fingers cradled the dryad's tiny green hand as if it were the most precious thing she had ever held.

"Mhm."

Elisabeth stood where she had been standing for the past several minutes, hands at her sides, staring at the scene with an expression that had stopped attempting to process new information roughly one weeping elf ago.

Being pampered by the Queen of All Elves and the head of their faith, both of whom were sobbing in the dirt like new mothers meeting their firstborn.
"I need to sit down..." the Arch Priestess whispered.
Right on cue, a chair of stone materialized beneath her, sweeping the Arch Priestess off her feet.
"..." Her eyes narrowed as she examined the Primordial Villain.

Her expression softened. She moved around a bit in her new chair until it was just right, leaned back, and enjoyed the show.
Alexios, arms loose at his side, watched the pile of elves and dryad. His expression was far too wry, for he understood the implications.
The elves were already treating him like a deity. Without seeing this creature.
If they did, he had no doubt all members of their race would become weeping messes just like their queen and lead shrine maiden.
The political implications were impossible to miss.
"That tree..." His attention drifted to the golden veins still pulsing in slow, warm rivers across the trunk. "...How?"
"Remember the Geim you had locked up in that cave at your military outpost in Greenvale?" Quinlan wasted no time, asking casually.
Alexios's heart rate spiked instantly, on the verge of bursting. "...No."

Quinlan's grin widened, far too sadistic. "Old friend, I'd dock that storm dude's pay if I were you. I sent my Pupcake to cause some ruckus and a gang of werewolves caught a whiff of her heavenly pheromones and lost their minds. We waltzed right through the chaos while the storm dude was giving speeches about honor and duty."
"NO!" Alexios's voice rose.
Quinlan paused for dramatic effect just long enough before adding, "We were barely level ten back then, by the way."
"ELYSIAR!"
The cities. Built with his stolen gold.
The multiracial settlement. Stocked with stolen slaves.
The cobblestones, the mansion, the bathhouse, all funded by his pillaged treasury.
And now the tree, the centerpiece of this compound, the creature that had reduced two of the continent's most powerful elves to sobbing in the dirt, had been taken from his own military outpost.
By a level ten nobody and a horny dogkin girl's scent.
"Is there a single thing you own that you didn't steal from me?!" the King of Vraven screamed.
"Hmm... let me see..." with theatrical motions, Quinlan began pondering the question, looking like it required a lot of thinking.
Alexios was a patient man, all things considered.
But this bastard...

On the ground before them, Rosie had discovered that Myrasyn's long ears were within reaching distance, and a small green hand was creeping toward one with the careful precision of a predator stalking prey.

She did nothing to stop it.
Instead...
She lowered her head and offered hers freely.
"Hya!" Rosie lunged, grabbing onto both women's ears at once, eliciting merry yelping.
At the same time, a soft hand landed on Alexios's head.
Or tried to. Felicity had to jump to reach him, and her fingers barely grazed his crown before gravity reclaimed her.
She jumped again and managed to pat quickly twice.
"It's okay, Father." Her voice was perfectly, devastatingly understanding. "You tried your best."
Alexios looked down at his daughter, then up at the man who seemed intent on bringing him to an early grave due to a deadly stroke, and the look on his face said everything.
Quinlan was no longer paying attention.
His gaze had shifted toward the distance, and the amusement drained from his face. "The girls are ready."
He flicked two fingers, and a [Warp Gate] tore open in the courtyard.
Ayame stepped through.
Her composure was set, katana at her hip, spine straight.
She looked like a woman ready to conduct business.
It was time to begin.

chapters.title: Chapter 1785 Proud Girls
paragraphs: Ayame crossed the courtyard to Quinlan's side with the winter dusk settling gold and violet over the compound, and behind her the [Warp Gate] widened, its shimmer stretching until the doorway stood wide enough for multiple people to pass through at once.
Then the family came home.
"Master!"
Blossom cleared the gate at a dead sprint, ears pinned flat with speed, and crossed thirty meters of courtyard in the time it took Quinlan to open his arms.
She hit his chest hard enough to spin him half a step, burrowed in, and looked up with her tail whipping the air behind her.
"Blossom organized the whole cleanup and counted all the supply crates and didn't bite a single prisoner even when one of them called Master ugly names!"
"Good girl."
The tail became a blur just as Quinlan mused, "You made quite the scene back there."
The blur stalled, and her ears folded back as she pressed her face harder into his chest.
Screaming a whole wolf lord halfway into the ground, in front of everyone, was not the sort of thing the bubbly dogkin was known for.
"...Blossom was very loud," she mumbled into his tunic.
One hand crept up from the fist it had made in his shirt and found the collar at her throat, closing around it with extreme tenderness.
Blossom didn't care about a lot of things.
"But the collar..."
Suggesting she gave it up?
That was entirely off limits.
Her thumb moved over the worn leather with far too soft of a touch, and her blue eyes went wet at the edges.
She tipped her head back to look up at him, chin still against his chest, and not a trace of the fury that had made Skarn flinch remained in her face.
"Is Master angry?" Her voice had gone tiny. "Blossom shouted, said mean things about the wolf's insecurities, cracked the ground, and made a scene at Master's important meeting in front of everyone."
Her ears sank lower. "Did Blossom make a mistake?"
Quinlan chuckled low in his chest and dipped his head until the tip of his nose brushed hers. "Angry? That was perhaps the most badass thing I've ever seen you do."
Then he paused, thinking. There were a lot of moments his electric, void-wielding, far too gorgeous dogkin lover achieved, so it was hard to claim a single moment as clearly above the rest.
He shrugged, settling for: "It's certainly up there."
The worry left her ears one degree at a time, and then all at once the tail burst back into a blur, fast enough to stir the hem of her clothes.
She surged onto her toes and kissed him, quick and reverent, dropping little presses to his cheek, his chin, the corner of his mouth, each one its own small thank-you and love-you.

He caught her waist to keep them both upright and grinned through it. "A short dogkin girl walked up to the alpha of the entire wolfkin tribe and made him look like a scared little puppy, in front of every soldier he commands."
His grin widened. "The dogkin are going to sing about that for generations. Pups who aren't even born yet are going to hear about the girl who out-howled the wolf lord."

Blossom, finally done delivering her barrage of needy kisses, hummed and burrowed into the side of his neck, her arms winding around him, her whole weight going trusting and boneless against his front.

"Blossom doesn't care about such things," she whispered into his skin, her tail still going behind her. Her arms tightened. "But if Master is proud of Blossom, then Blossom is the happiest girl in the whole wide world."
"Hubby~"
Vex arrived at his back rather than his front, and for once she didn't wrestle anyone for access to his front.

She wound both arms around his waist from behind, pressed her cheek flat between his shoulder blades, and settled in like she meant to be removed surgically or not at all, content to let the dog girl keep the embrace she'd earned.

"Did you see, hubby?" The words came muffled against his spine, thick with pride. "I didn't demand a single kiss the second I laid eyes on you. I let Blossom have you for as long as she needs. Because I know she deserved it."
She even went as far as to admit: "That was amazing, Blossom."
Quinlan shook his head, amused.
Unlike most of his other girls, Vex had not taken to the harem life quite as gracefully.
The early days had been a war she waged mostly against herself, and she'd lost more of those battles than she'd won, in ways that landed somewhere between pitiful and endearing.
There had been the night she sat down outside his bedroom door and cried her heart out while he was inside with someone else.
Quinlan hadn't minded her extreme jealousy.
He had never once minded.

He loved yanderes with a burning, uncomplicated passion. The only line he cared about was harem dynamics, and for all the times Vex had teetered right at the edge of causing real emotional problems for her fellow sister-wives with her possessive behavior, she had never once put a foot over the limit.
But clearing his bar for what was 'acceptable yandere behavior' had never been Vex's goal.
She'd set her own, and set it far higher.
She wanted to be his perfect wife, the woman who could stand by his side with extreme pride, and such wives did not wail on the doorstep while their husband saw to someone else.
So she'd been working at it, quiet and stubborn, filing down a jealousy that ran bone-deep.
Holding still at his back while he cradled another woman was one of those filings.
It mattered to her. And because it mattered to her, it mattered to him.

He loosened one arm from around Blossom, reached back, and drew Vex around to his side, gathering both girls in against him at once. Then he tipped her chin up and kissed her forehead. "I saw everything. My yandere witch is amazing as well."
Vex was already rising onto her toes to meet it before it landed, chasing the kiss up like she'd been waiting all her life.
"The queen of jealousy behaved like she was a member of a harem made of friends and not enemies to destroy," Aurora observed in passing, then began clapping.
*Clap. Clap. Clap.*
"Is this how mothers feel when their child finally stops pooping their pants?"
"..." Vex's eyes instantly narrowed into dangerous slits, aimed at a certain platinum haired, grinning girl.
Aurora only offered her a peace sign with her fingers in response.
Kitsara sauntered out next, five tails swaying in lazy arcs. "Stop badmouthing Vexie... I'm really proud of her!"
One tail detached only to form a second Quinlan, who began patting Vex's white hair.
But a kick to the stomach dispelled the illusion, as Vex scoffed, "Only the real version can touch me. I promised Hubby I'd never let another man lay his hands on me."
"..." The foxkin was speechless for a moment, which spoke volumes about the absurdity of what just left the Hexwitch's lips.
"That was-"
"Not my Hubby," Vex interjected.
"... No matter how you look at it, no other man was involved. It's either him or me, a woman..."

"No. How do I know you replicated him down to the very last atom? If a single detail, a single strand of hair is misplaced, then that's no longer an illusion of my Hubby but a replica of another man."
"What the fuck is wrong with you?" Kitsara asked, then burst into laughter, clutching her stomach. "Never change, you insane bitch," she decreed between breaths.

The rest poured through in a wave, Serika hauling a supply crate on one shoulder and laughing together with Kitsara, Seraphiel and Kaelira deep in conversation, Feng trailing at the rear with her hands shoved in her sleeves.
The courtyard filled with the noise of a family arriving somewhere it belonged.

Then they all stopped to take in the scene at the base of the giant tree, where the Queen of All Elves knelt in the dirt with tears running freely down her face while a small green girl inspected the royal ears held out for her approval.
Beside her queen, the Head Shrine Maiden of the elven faith sat with a dryad's foot in her lap.
She was massaging it.

"Rosie's new friends are very talented!" Rosie declared from her throne of elven laps, both arms spread in imperial welcome as the girls approached. "The pretty ladies have earned the right to keep serving!"
"Serving?" Jasmine inquired with far too big of a grin on her lips.
"!!" Rosie was caught. "Rosie meant pampering!"
"Mhm..." Jasmine nodded along.
Myrasyn mouthed the word "friends" to herself like a blessing and Isveth kept massaging while her tears increased in their intensity.

Lucille came through the gate last of the girls, stopped on the cobblestones, and simply breathed for a moment, taking in the pine, the woodsmoke, and the copper vent of the bathhouse trailing steam into the evening air.
"Our home keeps getting louder and louder," she said, but her tone held zero complaint, only firm approval.
The gate rippled again, and a different kind of arrival stepped through.

Scar walked out first, both blades at her back and her pace even, and behind her came the Scarlet Lilies, four women stepping onto foreign ground with careful, unaccustomed footing, mercenaries who had spent their careers arriving everywhere uninvited.
Bronnya made it three steps before her head tilted back, and kept tilting, and kept tilting, until her mouth hung open at the crown of golden light spreading against the first stars.
"That's... a tree," she managed.
"Are you sure it's not a bush...?" Void yawned.

The rest poured through in a wave, Serika hauling a supply crate on one shoulder and laughing together with Kitsara, Seraphiel and Kaelira deep in conversation, Feng trailing at the rear with her hands shoved in her sleeves.
The courtyard filled with the noise of a family arriving somewhere it belonged.

Then they all stopped to take in the scene at the base of the giant tree, where the Queen of All Elves knelt in the dirt with tears running freely down her face while a small green girl inspected the royal ears held out for her approval.
Beside her queen, the Head Shrine Maiden of the elven faith sat with a dryad's foot in her lap.
She was massaging it.
"Rosie's new friends are very talented!" Rosie declared from her throne of elven laps, both arms spread in imperial welcome as the girls approached.
"The pretty ladies have earned the right to keep serving!"
"Serving?" Jasmine inquired with far too big of a grin on her lips.
"!!" Rosie was caught.
"Rosie meant pampering!"
"Mhm..." Jasmine nodded along.
Myrasyn mouthed the word "friends" to herself like a blessing and Isveth kept massaging while her tears increased in their intensity.

Lucille came through the gate last of the girls, stopped on the cobblestones, and simply breathed for a moment, taking in the pine, the woodsmoke, and the copper vent of the bathhouse trailing steam into the evening air.
"Our home keeps getting louder and louder," she said, but her tone held zero complaint, only firm approval.
The gate rippled again, and a different kind of arrival stepped through.

Scar walked out first, both blades at her back and her pace even, and behind her came the Scarlet Lilies, four women stepping onto foreign ground with careful, unaccustomed footing, mercenaries who had spent their careers arriving everywhere uninvited.
Bronnya made it three steps before her head tilted back, and kept tilting, and kept tilting, until her mouth hung open at the crown of golden light spreading against the first stars.
"That's... a tree," she managed.
"Are you sure it's not a bush...?" Void yawned.

chapters.title: Chapter 1786 Sincere Words
paragraphs: "That's... a tree," she managed.
"Are you sure it's not a bush...?" Void yawned.

Lilith said nothing at all. While her comrades gawked upward, her eyes made one slow pass across the courtyard, over the pile of elves and children, over the girls, over the doorway of the mansion, hunting for the silhouette of a certain woman that wasn't among them. When she didn't find it, she turned back to the group.
"Do not climb the tree," Scar announced to the four of them, flat as a shipping manifest.
"Why would I climb the..." Bronnya started.
"The little lady dislikes strangers climbing her. You would be shaken out."
"...What? Little lady? Climb?"
Scar, with amused eyes, only nodded. "Yes."
The gate flared one final time, and the evening's strangest guest arrived.

Iris came through with a chain of dark iron wrapped twice around her fist, and at the other end of it, drifting along on a low sled of packed earth, stood a monolith of layered frost with a skull protruding from the top of it.

Gorthrax the Eternal had been encased in ice from the collarbones down, arranged upright like a museum exhibit, and the ember light in his sockets swept across the compound with unmistakable appreciation.

"Young lord of the dead!" His voice rolled out deep and warm, pitched for a dinner party rather than captivity. "What a magnificent seat you've built yourself. Normally it would've been better beneath the earth, but the tree alone justifies the decision to keep your domain above ground."
"..." Quinlan said nothing.
That did not bother the undead.
"The architecture shows restraint. Clearly, it was built to satisfy your wives who still breathe and care for aesthetics. But strangely, that does not make it hideous."
"You." Elisabeth's voice lost all the friendly edge it had gained during the tour and its many revelations. "Shut your mouth, filthy abomination."
The skull rotated a polite few degrees toward her. "Priestess. We meet again. You look well."
Iris yanked the chain, and the sled scraped on as the courtyard settled into the warm chaos of a homecoming.
Two elite souls who came through with the crowd held a woman between them.
Kaede Fujimori walked between her escorts on her own feet, but only just barely.
The healers had done their work, and the work had kept her alive, and nothing about the thin, colorless figure between the two dead soldiers suggested that being alive meant much to her.
Her eyes never left the ground. She looked at no one, asked for nothing, and passed through the middle of another family's homecoming as if the warmth around her were a language she'd never learned.
Ayame watched her sister for a long time.
Then Rosie's giggle floated up from the elf pile, high and bright, and the courtyard exhaled and remembered itself.
Felicity and Feng found each other by the food tables the maids had just brought out, exchanged the nod of two professionals, and executed a pincer maneuver on the dryad.
"Rosie," Felicity announced, kneeling to her level. "We've been sent to escort you to the kids' table. There are honey pastries."
"Rosie has servants- friends now," Rosie countered from between two elves. "Royal ones."
"The 'friends' are needed for grown-up business," Feng said, grinning at the shameless girl's antics.
Rosie gasped then patted Myrasyn's head twice with grave ceremony. "Rosie releases you. Attend to your business. Then return to Rosie."
"Yes, my lady," the Queen of All Elves said without waiting for a single moment.
The three children departed for the far table, and the adults began drifting toward the mansion as the night took full hold of the sky.
That was when Alexios spoke up.
"Before we proceed."
The noise died on its own.
Ayame turned to face him, and her spine was already straight.

"There is business waiting in that house, and I find I can't walk into it carrying what I'm carrying." The King of Vraven stood the way only an old king stands, and the exhaustion sitting openly on his face did not diminish that fact.
He looked Ayame in the eyes. "So I'll say it here, in front of your family. Delaying any further would be a slap to your face you do not deserve."
"When the Fujimori petition reached my desk, it was clean. Evidence, seals, sworn testimony, every page in order. I signed it between a grain tariff and a border report, and that was it."
His hands stayed at his sides.
"A king has reasons. We always do." He chuckled at that, but there was no amusement in it, only a bone-deep tiredness.

Then, he explained with a voice that carried zero conviction, "The dukes are powerful rulers who govern their ancestral lands while resisting every oversight from the throne. A crown that squeezes them breeds the very rebellion it fears. Distance is policy. Trust is procedure. I could stand here all night listing reasons, and every one of them would be true."
He paused, and for a moment the thousand-year-old king looked every hour of it.
"Yet not one of them matters to what was done to you."
Ayame held his gaze and offered him no help.
He continued anyway, and his voice stayed level through sheer discipline and nothing else.
"You were innocent. The kingdom that owed you its protection sold you at auction under my seal, because looking closer would have cost me."
He let the sentence end there, and the stop was audible. It had a second half, a price with a name, and every person in the courtyard heard it.

"You will learn what that cost was before this night is over, along with everything else the questioning drags into the open. When you do, understand this." He held Ayame's eyes. "It is only context and not a defense. I offer none."
The words came out measured, each one set down like a stone he'd carried too far.
"I was deceived, not because the plot was cunning, but because I allowed myself to be deceived."
Then Alexios Valorian, King of Vraven, bowed his head to an eternal slave.
"I am sorry."
At the edge of the gathering, Kaede's eyes lifted from the ground for the first time.
Elisabeth went rigid, the retort dying half-formed.
Around the courtyard, the girls had gone completely still, and Quinlan watched without a word, because this belonged to no one but the two people standing in the lantern light.
"The decree dies tonight," Alexios said, head still lowered. "Every record in Vraven that names you property will be struck and burned. Tonight, you, Ayame Fujimori, will be free and-"
"No."
The word came out gentle, and it stopped a king mid-decree.
At the arena she'd had to talk herself out of the tightness in her fingers when this man approached; now her hand rested easy on the katana's hilt.
Alexios's head stayed bowed. "...No?"
"Raise your head."
He did, slowly, and found her smiling.
"Don't call me Ayame Fujimori."
"You stripped me of legally wearing the Fujimori name in your kingdom. My legal name is Ayame. Thus you will call me Ayame."
The king straightened, and the ruler in him reached for the remedy he knew how to give. "Then the crown will reinstate you tonight. You will wear the Fujimori name with full legal standing and-"
Ayame tilted her head. "No. That's not what I meant."
"I have no use for a clan's name that tossed me away, especially now that I have a family of my own. So..."
Her smile widened, content and wholesome. "Until the day I legally wear my lover's name, just Ayame will do."
Alexios went still, holding her gaze for a long second, and then another, the word turning over behind his eyes.
Lover, not husband.
Then the King of Vraven laughed under his breath.

"So be it." He inclined his head to her once more. "My sin will never be repaid no matter what I do, and I won't insult you by trying. But if you would accept one small gesture from an old fool... when the day comes, the Valorian crown will fund that wedding, however grand it needs to be, so the name you desire arrives the way you deserve."
For a moment, Ayame simply looked at him.
Then the composed second-in-command gave the King of Vraven a grin with teeth in it, one hundred percent her lover's brand.
"Ready your coffers, old man. And I want your screeching daughter to grant our union the Goddess's blessing."
"Eh?" Elisabeth gasped.
"...Deal," Alexios decreed, his mouth crooking. "I'll do my utmost to gain the church's approval."
"Eh???" Elisabeth gasped again, stronger.
"Good." Ayame nodded.

She had never forgiven the king, any more than she'd forgiven Kaede, and no such words left the samurai's delicate lips. She only wanted to move on and live the life she desired; demanding blood from people already repenting served no one.
Numerous grins broke out around the courtyard, and more than one of the girls made a sound suspiciously close to a squeal.
Quinlan said nothing, but no one looked prouder than he did in that moment.
Ayame let the smile settle back into composure and turned for the mansion. "Now come, everyone. Let's find out what those treacherous sacks of bones have been hiding all these years."
The group funneled out of the lantern light and through the mansion doors, family and guests alike.
High above them, behind the one window left open to the winter night, a silhouette sat motionless against the stars, waiting in the room she had prepared.

chapters.title: Chapter 1787 Serenity Under The Moonlight
paragraphs: Black Fang had chosen the room herself.
Third floor, at the top of the last staircase.

The wide hall with the tall windows that nobody in the household had ever found a use for, meant for events never thrown as they were far too busy, furnished with chairs that collected dust until tonight.
She had cleared it down to bare floor, and the two blocks of ice stood alone in the center with the frozen faces of the last Fujimori elders staring out of them.
Quinlan reached the top of the stairs first and stopped.
'Damn...'

Moonlight fell through the tall windows and pooled silver across the floorboards and the ice. Rosie's otherworldly, fairy tale-like tree's crown pulsed its slow gold beyond the glass, and the frozen elders stood at the center of it all as if the room had been built around them.
'This woman... Why is she always so mesmerizing?'

On the sill of the farthest window, one boot drawn up and the other hanging into the dark, Black Fang sat watching the sky. Winter stars burned sharp and close above the treeline, and the light traced the line of her profile, the violet eyes at rest, the serpent tattoos asleep along her arms.
"Why drag them all the way up here? There's room next to the other lovely guests we house..." Quinlan mused. "Could've just put them in there."
Black Fang kept her gaze on the beautiful moonlight for a long second, silent. Then her eyes left the sky for the first time and found his. They carried a strange, muted light.
"So that I can wait in the basement for hours while you show off?"
Quinlan smirked instantly at that.
Her gaze held his amused eyes a beat longer, and then the edge left as she returned to watching the stars. "No."
One by one, the rest filed in behind him and went quiet without being asked. Even Elisabeth, arriving mid-complaint about seating an abomination indoors, lost the sentence somewhere on the threshold.
Isveth stopped dead beside her queen. "..." Her hand found Myrasyn's sleeve, and the two elves stared at the woman in the window with an expression usually reserved for shrines.
Kaede sat small in the far corner between her two escorts, her hands slack in her lap, watching the floor.
Quinlan looked at the mesmerizing assassin a moment longer, at the extreme serenity she wore without effort, and then he turned to the two monuments in the moonlight and flicked two fingers.
The frost sheeted off Chizuru's block and shattered across the floorboards.
"..." Chizuru blinked ice water out of her eyes.

She took in the moonlight, the ring of watching faces, the window full of stars, the villain standing before her with his hands calmly at his sides, and the last echo of her own defiance hanging in a room that had no audience to perform it for.
"Welcome back," Lucille greeted pleasantly.
"..." The fire went out of the elder's face the way it had in the arena, all at once and from the center, and what remained was a grey, flat emptiness.
Quinlan flicked his fingers again, and the second block cracked open.

The eldest of the Fujimori elders drew one long breath through his nose and straightened his spine as the ice fell away from him, with a slow dignity that his soaked robes did their best to undermine. His gaze passed over the villain and the king as if they were furniture, caught on the broken heir in the corner, and his lip curled a fraction.
Then his eyes settled on Chizuru, and they held less mercy than the ice he'd just left.
"You gave them everything?!"
"We lost..." Chizuru said to the floor.
"Silence is always an option!"
"Silence." Chizuru laughed once, a dry, terrible little sound with no humor in it. "You think they will let me remain silent?"
Hozumi turned to the wall instead of answering, and the two last elders of the Fujimori stood in a puddle of their own melting prison while the space between them did the talking.

"For what it's worth, she did not give us everything," Quinlan told the elder as he pulled a chair from the wall with a current of wind, turned it backward, and sat down astride it with his arms folded across the backrest, comfortable as a man settling in for a card game.
"So let us resume," he said, his gaze on Chizuru. "The arena heard what your clan did. Tonight I want the why. Elvardia's war first. Why did you join them?"
"The clan does not answer to its captors!" Hozumi hissed. "Chizuru, don't you dare say another word."

"I see." Quinlan raised one finger, and ice began climbing back up Hozumi's body, slow and measured, crystalline sheets sealing around his shins, his waist, his chest. Then the casing swelled outward, thickening, the walls expanding until a gap opened between frost and skin.
"Thankfully, I only need one of you."

Veins of magma bled through the ice from the outside, glowing orange threads that burrowed through the frozen walls and met the water pooling within, and the temperature inside the casing climbed past scalding in seconds.
Despite being a level 74 powerhouse with a Vitality high enough to shrug off what would desecrate a normal human body...
"W-what is this?! STOP!" Hozumi's composure shattered as steam erupted against the inner walls and his robes fused to blistering skin.

Where a vein of magma ran too close to the surface, the flesh peeled back in thin wet strips that curled away into clouded water, and his hands clawed uselessly at ice that rebuilt from the outside faster than the heat could eat it from within.
Quinlan's ability to wreak havoc went far beyond what a 'normal human body' could take.
Now, he was powerful enough to cause agonizing pain even for the continent's apex beings.
"CHIZURU!" Hozumi's voice cracked, half drowned. "Fujimori honor is EVERYTHING! You will NOT speak willingly to these-"
The ice sealed over his mouth.

His muffled screaming carried on behind the frost, thin and wretched, and the casing shuddered with every thrash while the orange glow of the magma pulsed through the ice in slow, steady rhythms, turning the elder's prison into a furnace with a window.

Quinlan hadn't moved from his chair for a single moment throughout this brutal display of cruelty. His chin rested on his folded arms, and nothing in his expression had changed since he spoke his question to Chizuru, his eyes remaining on the female elder.
Elisabeth stared at the man she had apologized to, and the expression on her face was far too difficult to read.
She turned away.
In the seconds that followed, accompanied by thrashing inside a magma-filled ice casing lacking in oxygen, everyone in the room understood why the children had been sent away.
Quinlan, despite his calm exterior, was carrying immense anger toward these human garbage. He had no intention of playing nice.
As for why they were still not [Subjugated]?
Simply because Hozumi was Alexios's prey while Chizuru was Black Fang's.
There was a creed among sadistic torturers such as them...
Though he had no reservations about enslaving either elder should they refuse to comply.
