"Thankfully, I only need one of you."

Veins of magma bled through the ice from the outside, glowing orange threads that burrowed through the frozen walls and met the water pooling within, and the temperature inside the casing climbed past scalding in seconds.
Despite being a level 74 powerhouse with a Vitality high enough to shrug off what would desecrate a normal human body...
"W-what is this?!
STOP!" Hozumi's composure shattered as steam erupted against the inner walls and his robes fused to blistering skin.

Where a vein of magma ran too close to the surface, the flesh peeled back in thin wet strips that curled away into clouded water, and his hands clawed uselessly at ice that rebuilt from the outside faster than the heat could eat it from within.
Quinlan's ability to wreak havoc went far beyond what a 'normal human body' could take.
Now, he was powerful enough to cause agonizing pain even for the continent's apex beings.
"CHIZURU!" Hozumi's voice cracked, half drowned.
"Fujimori honor is EVERYTHING!
You will NOT speak willingly to these-"
The ice sealed over his mouth.

His muffled screaming carried on behind the frost, thin and wretched, and the casing shuddered with every thrash while the orange glow of the magma pulsed through the ice in slow, steady rhythms, turning the elder's prison into a furnace with a window.
Quinlan hadn't moved from his chair for a single moment throughout this brutal display of cruelty.
His chin rested on his folded arms, and nothing in his expression had changed since he spoke his question to Chizuru, his eyes remaining on the female elder.
Elisabeth stared at the man she had apologized to, and the expression on her face was far too difficult to read.
She turned away.
In the seconds that followed, accompanied by thrashing inside a magma-filled ice casing lacking in oxygen, everyone in the room understood why the children had been sent away.
Quinlan, despite his calm exterior, was carrying immense anger toward these human garbage.
He had no intention of playing nice.
As for why they were still not [Subjugated]?
Simply because Hozumi was Alexios's prey while Chizuru was Black Fang's.
There was a creed among sadistic torturers such as them...
Though he had no reservations about enslaving either elder should they refuse to comply.

chapters.title: Chapter 1788 The Why
paragraphs: In the corner, Kaede flinched. However, she did not do so because of Quinlan's display of cruelty.
'Fujimori honor is everything.'

She had heard those words in council chambers, at formal dinners, whispered into her ear before every test the elders designed. She looked up from the floor and watched the most honorable man her clan had ever produced writhe for air as his skin melted.
Chizuru didn't look at him. She stared at the floor, and nothing in her posture changed.

"You had Silverwind," Ayame spoke up, returning to the topic at hand. "You were building toward taking Greenvale in the competition, and you were doing well. If you focused on that and won, then you just needed a few years to consolidate your powers, wait for the old man to kick the bucket, and you'd wield more power than the crown itself."
"..." Alexios couldn't help but send the young oriental lady a wry glance. But then he returned his attention to Chizuru, knowing she was entirely correct.
The topic of Succession has been on his mind for a very, very long time.
Numerous powers were making moves with his encroaching death in mind, not just the Fujimori because, for various reasons, none of his heirs were ready to inherit the throne.
The Vraven Kingdom was facing its most difficult years as soon as he died.

Ayame did not seem to recognize or care for the old king's attention on her, however, as she asked, "Why throw all of it away to join Elvardia's side? You must've known the crown would learn of your treason and all your effort would be ruined."

"'Your?'" Something crept into Chizuru's voice, thin and instinctive, and the dead register shifted by a fraction. "Why do you keep saying 'your' and not 'our?' You can hate us all you want, children, but you," at that she paused, gaze going from Ayame to Black Fang, "both of you, are Fujimori."
Black Fang offered no reaction, save for a dark smile, but Ayame was different. Every trace of the composed magistrate left her face.
She couldn't believe the endless hypocrisy this woman kept spewing whenever she got the chance.
"If you dare say that I-" her eyes went to the window, to Black Fang still watching the serene moonlight, "-or she, belong to the Fujimori one more time, I will show you the real meaning of pain."
"She's already slated for years of agony..." Black Fang spoke up suddenly, voice soft, nonchalant. "But you're welcome to join."

Ayame's anger dissipated quickly as she heard the invitation, expression replicating her sadistic big sister's ominous smile. "...That's certainly one way to bond with your sister. But now you ruined my threat."
"It was a weak threat. She already knows what I'll do to her," Black Fang explained calmly, educating her little sister in the art of threats. "The threat of you joining me won't make her behave."
"..." Ayame's eyes narrowed as she observed Chizuru and noted how she was still a free woman. Then understanding shone through.

For the woman who had ruled an entire duchy from the shadows, the loss of control, the ultimate loss of control... "I'll have you enslaved and ordered by my partner to speak all we want to hear right away without your chatter."
Black Fang said nothing, but that in itself was approval.
Chizuru's mouth closed, eyeing Quinlan with gnawing fear.

"These emotional manipulation tricks might have worked on Kaede." Ayame smiled, seeing she understood how this trash bag's brain worked. "But they won't work here. They just make me even more disgusted with you."
"..." Chizuru slowly lowered her head, staring at the floor.
The manipulation was gone from Chizuru's voice when she finally answered.

"The reason we didn't wait is because we couldn't. The competition was never the end goal." Her voice came out stripped bare. "Greenvale was just a stepping stone. The blade demanded that its wielder stand above all of Iskaris. As you have understood, our original plan was to go from one duchy to two and then reshape the kingdom from the inside until we controlled it all. Then would come the rest of Iskaris..."
Everyone looked at Alexios, wondering what he thought about this revelation, if he knew.
The king sat very still, grim yet unsurprised.
"But the plan was built for a world without that thing." Chizuru's gaze found Quinlan, and the dead register cracked. "This abomination's existence changed everything."

Quinlan grinned at that, but his stalwart samurai did not find the way he was spoken of amusing. Her jaw tightened at the ugly word spoken with extreme disgust, but before she could, a voice came from the window.
"There are degrees to suffering."
Black Fang still hadn't turned from the stars. The words arrived soft and unhurried, yet they brought with them an immense sense of dread.
Chizuru's mouth snapped shut, and the defiance that had crept back evaporated.
Her attention darted to the serene silhouette in the window, and the fear that crossed her face had nothing to do with ice or subjugation.
Ayame looked at her sister's back, at the profile that hadn't shifted a single inch, and shook her head.

She would have needed cold steel in her voice and a hand on her hilt to land half of that. Black Fang had done it with a few words and the view of her back. 'She truly is terror in the flesh. Amazing...'
The oriental beauty refocused on Chizuru. "His existence forced your hand. Now I understand why you called him a cruel joke of the Goddess."
Chizuru was silent for a long moment, then dipped her chin.
"We watched him grow," she said, thin and bitter, and her eyes began moving from face to face as she spoke. "First it was the princess."

Her gaze landed on Alexios, and anger flared through the emptiness, brief and hot. "The Villain, using the chance to endear himself to Felicity, managed to form a bond with the king himself, despite the two men being enemies who kept trying to kill each other. By the time we turned traitor, the two of them were bantering like best friends and the princess was clearly attached to the Villain."
Alexios didn't move.
"Then the foxkin." Her eyes slid to Kitsara. "A princess of the Beastman Confederation. Through her, he had presence among an entire nation that should have been beyond his reach."
Kitsara waved at the old woman, carefree.

"And then the elves." Chizuru's gaze reached Myrasyn and Isveth, and the thin voice broke into open fury, the defeated puppet snapping its strings for one raw moment. "Their Queen, openly flirting with him on the battlefield. Their faith's head maiden, weeping at his feet. Their race, choosing him over everything they'd built across millennia."
Myrasyn held her gaze, regal and unmoved. Isveth looked proud at the words spoken of her.

"We saw the writing on the wall." The anger drained from Chizuru as quickly as it had come, leaving her flatter than before. "If we kept playing the long game, he would swallow the continent before we ever could. So we abandoned everything we'd spent generations building and joined Elvardia, the last real resistance standing between the Villain and enough political control and personal might to consume it all."
Her eyes dropped to the floor. "Together, using Kaede's dimensional movement ability to ambush him, we should have been strong enough to end his reign of terror before it even truly began."
The room sat with that.
Then, from the window:
"Why did the blade need a continent?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1789 The Truth
paragraphs: "Why did the blade need a continent?"
Black Fang asked, still observing the serene night sky.
"..." Chizuru said nothing.
The silence held past composure and became refusal.
Ayame cleared her throat. "Khm."
It was a small, almost polite sound, and the elder's gaze snapped to her as though the samurai had drawn steel.
Then Chizuru's eyes found Quinlan, and whatever she read in the way he was looking at her finished what remained of her resistance.
"I'm sorry, Black Fang. I wanted to not taint your prey more than needed, but..." he mused, chin resting on his folded arms.
"What a gentleman," Black Fang murmured. Then she finally looked away from the window, feet landing on the floor, sitting on the windowsill. "I don't mind."
"I always am a gentleman. Just ask my grandmother."
"T-t-the First Elf has a mother?!" Myrasyn and Isveth broke into a shocked squeal in sync.
"..." Quinlan's expression turned sour. He meant his human grandmother who kept calling him a real gentleman when he was a little kid.
"Quin, how about you stop flirting with my sister and the elves when we're interrogating the people who killed my father and wanted to do the same to me as well?" Ayame asked dryly.

Black Fang's eyes didn't look amused as she observed her little sister. At the same time, the two elves, amid rapid ear twitches, returned to their prior graceful stance, electing to begin the inquisition into the truth when the occasion was right.
Quinlan, pretending not to have heard his beloved samurai's admittedly ever so slightly justified scoff, began casting.
"[Subju-]"
The words left Chizuru instantly.

"The ancestral instructions were simple!" Her voice came out rapid and miserable as she recited doctrine because the alternative had just been named aloud. "Five main duties are passed to the council of elders from the ancestors. Lead the clan to prosperity. Retain authority over the clan leader. Search, always, for a proper heir to the blade. When one is found, awaken it." She swallowed. "And listen to it."

"Attached to the five was a promise. If the elders fulfilled their duties and the wielder obeyed, the Fujimori would reign supreme, the barrier would fall, and the clan would enter its golden age." Her eyes came up from the floor, and for once there was nothing in them to decode. "That is the inheritance. No reason was ever written down for us, and the blade speaks to no one but its wielder."
"We were taught how to serve it. Never what its goals were."
Quinlan studied her for a long moment.

"So the clan that killed its own patriarch, rigged a succession, and spent longer than living memory burrowing into a foreign kingdom did all of it on instructions nobody alive has ever understood the purpose of."
"Now you understand what honor demands of a Fujimori," Chizuru said, and the absence of irony in it was the worst part.
'This blade again...'
Quinlan turned his hand over, and the obsidian relic slid from his pocket ring into his grip.
The entire room leaned toward the weapon in one quiet, curious motion.
Quinlan raised the blade into the ring of moonlight and turned it slowly by the hilt.
In the arena it had fought him the entire way, hunger boring into his palm, veins darkening to the elbow while it searched for a way inside him.
Tonight the obsidian edge caught the moonlight and did nothing at all. He might as well have been holding a fire poker.
In the corner, Kaede's breathing went shallow.

Since the succession, that voice had lived at the edge of her hearing, wanting, promising, weighing. Now the sword that had decided her entire life sat ten paces away in the hand of the man who had broken it, and it did not stir for her.
The quiet where its whisper used to live was the loudest thing in the room.
It was Ayame who spoke next.
"Why did you have to kill Raijin Fujimori exactly? Just so Kaede could inherit the clan as soon as possible?"
The question landed without decoration, and Chizuru didn't ask who she meant.

"...That's a part of it, yes. The other part is the binding. To awaken the blade in a new wielder is said to be a great risk." Chizuru recited. "To ensure higher chances of success, sacrificing the wielder's strongest living bloodline member was required. Two birds with one stone."
"So he was material for your ritual..." Ayame's hands closed into fists at her sides, and she held them there for a long time while the room gave her the silence she needed.
"Is he still in there?" The words came out rough.
Chizuru opened her mouth, but a different voice answered first.
"I don't believe that he is."
Every head in the room turned toward the corner.
Kaede hadn't moved, and her voice was so thin it barely carried past the healers on either side of her.
She was looking at the floor, her hands gripping the fabric at her wrist, twisting it tight.
"The being who spoke to me in the blade... it wasn't Father." She swallowed, and the sound was audible. "It never sounded like him. It never remembered what he remembered."
Ayame looked at her sister for a long time, and the composure she'd worn all evening wavered at the edges.
"Did it tell you what it really wanted? Why it needed to conquer at the cost of risking everything?"
Kaede's teeth found her lower lip. "That to unlock its full power, I had to become the ruler of Iskaris."
"...That's it?"
Kaede flinched at that, visibly shrinking in her chair.

Ayame sighed, but pressed on. "And when you rule? Is something supernatural supposed to happen? It can't just be about corrupted ego and whatnot, right? I'm trying to understand why it wanted to risk everything to prevent Quinlan from taking over."
Kaede bit harder, and a thin line of blood welled on her lip and ran down her chin.
Her voice came through gritted teeth, wet and raw.

"I don't know." The tears arrived with the admission. "It said conquer. I asked why and it said to bring about the golden age of my people. I asked what would happen and it told me I would understand when I was worthy."
Her hand came up to cover her face, and what was left of her composure broke. "I did everything it asked, and I never understood any of it, and I'm sorry, I'm sorry..."
Ayame stood where she was, and for several seconds she simply had nothing.
Seeing the emotional turmoil his partner in crime was dealing with, Quinlan spoke. Level and unhurried, still turning the dead blade between his fingers.
"The blood of the father to awaken it. The severance of the bond with the sister to feed it."

He tilted the obsidian edge until it caught the moonlight flat, gaze on Chizuru. "And that rite you performed on the battlefield... When you lifted your talisman and chanted about the blood of your ancestors, and hundreds of your own clan withered into husks where they stood. Everything they had went straight into this."
He looked at Chizuru over the relic's edge. "What's the mechanism behind it all?"

"...Aside from experience points, the blade feeds also from its wielder's hand, on what its wielder owns... And at a much faster rate than XP normally would allow. That's why Kaede had to become the clan leader, and the undisputed one at that..." Chizuru's gaze drifted to Kaede. No apology lived anywhere in it.
"That doesn't quite answer my question," Quinlan replied.

chapters.title: Chapter 1790 A Bribed King
paragraphs: "...I don't know the exact mechanics, Villain. When we gave the blade what it demanded, it grew more powerful. And in the case of the sacrifice I orchestrated back then, it could momentarily go beyond its current capabilities."
"A feeding mechanism that grows on sacrifice," Quinlan concluded with a nod.
Alexios spoke without moving his eyes from the blade.
"The concoction your clan brewed for me." His voice went careful. "Was it also fed with..."

Chizuru chuckled, and it was the ugliest sound she'd made all night. "Does it disgust you now, Your Majesty? Knowing what touched the very thing that kept you alive? Yes, we fed you the blood of massacred orphans-"
"Alright, I'm done," Quinlan sighed.
Every speck of mockery left the old woman's face as if it never existed. "Wait-"
"[Subjugation]."
Chizuru's body seized on the spot. The scream that left her was raw and graceless.
"Please, I spoke out of turn, I'll-"

"You'll answer every question put to you fully and honestly, without embellishing, withholding, or acting like... You," he spoke with extreme disgust, fully done listening to this bottomless pit of hypocrisy. "Now answer his question properly."

Despite her best effort, despite her frantic eyes, she began monologuing instantly. "We didn't lie to you back then. The recipe used exotic, rare materials that don't exist on this continent. We only have a finite collection of them, brought in by the ancestors when they arrived on the continent... It's then prepared by a Fujimori alchemist with inherited technique. No blood of orphans was involved."
Quinlan looked at Alexios.

"'You will die of old age within months at the latest.'" He quoted it casually. "She screamed that at you on the battlefield while you were trying to cut her head off. Want to fill in the rest, old friend?"
"..." Alexios exhaled, tense, finally looking like a man who was a millennium old.
"The Fujimori approached me a few years ago with a concoction no one on the continent could replicate. Alchemy from what they called their clan's ancient, outside records."
Aurora instantly perked up upon hearing that.
Alexios's voice carried no performance. "It promised to slow the aging, letting me continue to breathe past the natural human limit of around a thousand years by up to a whole century."
He chuckled, shaking his head while adding, "So long as I kept taking it, of course."
Every person in the room turned toward the old king.
It was a great mystery how the old king remained alive at his age, let alone this powerful.
Even humans at his level should've experienced a rapid decline as their natural lifespan ran out, deteriorating with extreme speed in their last few years.
Alexios, while showing obvious signs of aging, was not at all even at the start of the rapid decline stage. He was still in his prime.

"And they promised I wouldn't be dependent on them for the full duration of that century because they had a way to take down the Heavenly Restriction," Alexios continued. "When it fell, I could level past seventy-four and extend my lifespan naturally without taking more of their potions."
He paused, expression full of clarity.

"That was only a few years before the blade was awakened. Now it's clear that they were preparing me to look the other way when it did, not investigating or worse. All I had to do was keep out of their business and I'd get to live forever."
He exhaled through his nose.
"It was too clean a trap to fight, and if I did die, the prowling vultures would've descended on my heir. So I took their offer, knowing it was in my family's best interest that I stayed in power."

Quinlan's expression shifted, and genuine disappointment replaced the humor. "I feared you for months, old man. Lost sleep over how to handle the strongest human alive." He shook his head, deflated. "And you were taking bribes all along? Being a good boy to these wretches?"
Alexios's fist clenched in response, and for a moment the room held still, Alexios visibly deciding whether to settle this with his hands.
Quinlan really knew how to get under his skin.
"Haaah..." Then he exhaled again, and his fingers opened.
"You're right to be disappointed. I don't deserve to be feared by an unfair existence such as you." The words came out steady.

"I'm just a mortal man at the end of his lifespan, with heirs too young or too weak to hold the throne, and powerful dukedoms who've been positioning for my death since before I was even born. Of course I knew the Fujimori were scheming. But as I said, me staying alive was in the best interest of the Valorian family. So I took their offer and played the dependent king."
Quinlan's eyes lit up as he heard the words spoken, and the tone with which they were uttered.
This was not how a hopelessly blackmailed person would speak.
Quinlan's grin returned, knowing that the crazed old fucker was too much of a badass to be such a pathetic loser. "...And?"
"They thought they had me leashed. Terrified of losing my supply."
The tired eyes went sharp, and behind them a plan that had been running for a long time showed its edge. "So I let them think it. I took their potions and..."

His eyes found Ayame. "...Looked the other way. I didn't interfere with their internal affairs, nor did I investigate Kaede. Normally, I would've sent my enforcers, knowing that something foul was at play. I wouldn't have let an eighteen year old girl grow this powerful this quickly without ensuring she wasn't a threat to the crown."
Ayame tensed up hearing the admission. The king did say she'd learn more of why he did what he did in this talk, but...
It wasn't easy on her. That was when, to her surprise, a dozen voices sounded in her head almost in perfect sync.
Her friends were all telling her to keep it together, that it's okay, that they're here for her.
"..." A soft smile appeared on her lips.

"And while every scheming duchy in my kingdom positioned themselves for my eventual death, using the extra time I was given, I made my own preparations," Alexios went on. "I knew I had to clean house, to cripple the strength of the families who'd been plotting for generations to rebel against the Valorian blood."
The shock on Chizuru's face was total.
He was making his own play? All this time? While he was pretending to be perfectly blackmailed?!
"My goal was never to live forever," Alexios decreed, looking the Fujimori elder right in the eyes.

Then the sharpness left his features as quickly as it had come, and what remained was a father. "It was to die at the right time, in a kingdom clean enough for my children to inherit without old blood scheming behind their backs. I've spent a lifetime forced to maneuver around their whims and desires, unable to steer the nation in the direction I thought best because of their constant resistance. Thus, my final act was supposed to leave behind a nation worth inheriting. Then I could die feeling satisfied with the thought that I wasn't just another Valorian ruler who kept the status quo up."
Then he turned to Quinlan, and the expression was so dry it could have caught fire.
"But then an unknown nobody had to walk out of the woods and start eating the board I worked hard to set up."

chapters.title: Chapter 1791 Leaving Thalorind
paragraphs: "But then an unknown nobody had to walk out of the woods and start eating the board I worked hard to set up."
Quinlan grinned at the old king, and the grin held no remorse whatsoever.
"My sincerest apologies."
"Your apologies are worth less than the oaths my dukes take, you infuriating bastard," Alexios grumbled, though the corner of his mouth twitched toward a shape he'd rather die than call a smile.
He composed himself, straightening, and swept the moonlit room with practiced calm. "I must say, you've shown remarkable restraint regarding Black Fang's claim on the elder."
His attention drifted to the ice casing where Hozumi's thrashing kept up with admirable determination despite the magma pulsing through the frost in slow, cruel rhythms.
"But what about mine?"
Quinlan tilted his head, not understanding. "What about him?"
"..." Alexios looked at him for a long second.
Then he sighed. "It's fine. Just make sure he's recognizable."
"Sure." Quinlan nodded along nicely. "Patching him back up will be a nice exercise for the healers."
"..." Alexios couldn't believe how this foul creature could somehow keep getting more and more shameless than he already was.
Quinlan turned back to the obsidian blade resting across his palm, turning it in the moonlight.
"Potion-gulping geezer." He turned the blade again, watching the moonlight slide off the edge without resistance. "Is it just me, or are the Fujimori useless? They know nothing of importance."
Alexios looked ready to slap the back of his head.
"...I must agree, you foul-mouthed brat. It appears they were all puppets of their ancestors' will."
Quinlan looked at Ayame.

She met his stare instantly, because she'd been watching the blade since the moment it came out, and the composure she wore for the room thinned by a fraction as his question arrived without him needing to say most of it.
"Do you mind?"
She looked at the obsidian edge. The blade that had drunk her father's blood to awaken. The blade whose voice, according to Kaede, had never sounded like him.
But she instantly knew the answer to her partner's question.
"Even if he's in there," she said quietly, "it's worth trying."
"..." Kaede's tears only flew stronger upon hearing the choice her big sister had made, how little she cared about her family that once was.
But she could not fault her for it.
Quinlan's smile for his samurai was the real one, warm and full of a pride he'd never once bothered hiding.
Then he stood in one sharp motion. "I need to get this piece of junk speaking, but I can't do it here."
"Do you need a smithy?" Myrasyn asked. "I can guide you to the royal dwarven smithy."

"No, I need a specific someone to help me," Quinlan spoke mysteriously, causing the elf queen to perk her ears. Then, Quinlan added a beat later, "I'll take you up on your offer later, though. There must be a lot of goodies there."
"...Alright," Myrasyn giggled.
Quinlan then turned toward the human king. "Old bastard, take a few deep breaths before we go in there. I'm afraid your heart might give out."
"In where?" Alexios rose with a scowl.
Quinlan raised his palm and pulled.
The air split.
A seam of pale light opened where nothing had been, and beyond it hung a sky full of stars that no navigator on this continent had ever charted, low and close and achingly still.
"In there."
"This... This is different than [Warp Gate]!" Myrasyn yelped, flabbergasted at what she was seeing. "Such an otherworldly magic..."
"You have great intuition." Quinlan smiled, then looked at the remaining guests.

Iris had already taken Gorthrax downstairs to interrogate him about her family and the Covenant's role in what happened to them. Black Fang stood at the edge of the seam, ready to walk right into the portal, her prisoner left behind in the corner.
His eyes found Elisabeth first, then moved on to the Scarlet Lilies, and a half-apology touched his face. "This part is private. I'm sorry."
Void's head rose from Bronnya's shoulder. "...I would like to see."
"Maybe later."
Her half-lidded gaze drifted to Elisabeth, displeased. "The screecher gets to go in, but we can't?"
"Hah?" Elisabeth's eyes narrowed at the mage.
"She's a fanatic of the Goddess," Quinlan said to Void, ignoring Elisabeth completely. "I might not like her one bit, but I know she won't give me trouble in the future."
"The feeling is mutual, Villain. And why are you so sure I won't harm you?" Elisabeth threatened, voice low.
The corner of Quinlan's mouth lifted, still leaving the Dawn Breaker on 'read' as he explained, "You ladies, however, I'm not fully certain of."

Quinlan was thinking about the very distant future here. His soul realm could not be attacked by mortals like the Lilies, but if they switched sides and fed intel to a hostile god, Quinlan could be in trouble.
Frankly, he didn't know exactly how secretive he should be, feeling it was rather safe to show the realm. That's why he allowed Alexios and the elves to enter.
But there was no real drawback to keeping the Lilies outside.

Inviting them into his home and letting them listen in on their talks was already a great showing of courtesy, as far as he was concerned. Especially considering their history with him and his family.
"Protect our home in my absence?" he asked for a favor instead.
Void's pout deepened into a feat of facial architecture. "...Protect your home in your absence."
She surveyed the moonlit room through half-open lids, the puddles of melted ice, the slumped elder, the broken girl in the corner. "From what?"
Quinlan smirked and stepped through the seam without answering.
One by one, they followed, and the pale light sealed shut behind them.
"He ignored me..." Void muttered into the quiet that remained, in utter disbelief.
"How does a taste of your own medicine feel?" Jallen asked, smiling at her whiny friend. Void was the personification of selective hearing, so she really didn't have any right to complain.
"This is because we kept being antagonistic toward him," Void kept going on, eyes on Lilith while ignoring Jallen's words.

The Spellblade didn't look at her friend as she spoke with a voice holding zero sincerity. "Forgive me for not trusting the man literally called Primordial Villain who just happens to be the killer of our friend."

"Hmph. Bad Lilith..." Void did not forgive. She shifted from Bronnya's shoulder to Scar's side, settling against the blue-skinned woman. "Put in a good word for us, please..." She paused. "Or at least for me..."
"Hey." Bronnya looked at the shoulder Void had just vacated, wry.
Void did not hear her.
The soul realm opened around them.
"What the hell..." Alexios murmured under his breath.
Soft grassland rolled away under a sky of burning stars, closer and denser than any constellation on the continent, arranged in patterns no astronomer had charted.
The air carried no temperature and tasted clean in a way that made the room they'd left feel stale.

At the heart of it all, a tree rose from the soil with a pale trunk and faintly luminous leaves, roots curled protectively into the earth. Demonic vines wound through its bark in slow helical paths, pulsing with a soft pink light that made the whole thing look like a shrine with a heartbeat.
A small blue figure sat on the lowest branch with her feet dangling, and the moment the group appeared, both tiny arms went up.
"Scary Uncle! Everyone! Welcome back!"

Mimi launched from the branch and landed squarely in Serika's arms, burrowing into the redhead's chest with full-body enthusiasm, and Serika caught her without breaking stride, settling the little dryad against her shoulder with a gentleness she reserved for very few things in this world.
"Missed you too, little one."
Jasmine appeared from behind Serika's shoulder. "Grah!" She pounced on the blue girl with a scary snarl, fingers reaching Mimi's ribs before the dryad registered the ambush.

"EEEP!!" The shriek was instantaneous. Mimi thrashed, blue skin flushing violet, and scrambled up Serika's frame until she was clinging to her neck from behind with all four limbs. "P-protect me big sis Serika!!"
"Jasmine is a good girl..." Serika chuckled. "She's also very weak without her summons..."
Mimi only shook her head in response frantically and hid even further behind her sister.
"There's two of these wonderful existences?!" Isveth yelped. Myrasyn was no better. "And she's even smaller than Rosie?! My heart will melt...!"
Then the pressure arrived.

It came from everywhere at once, falling from the sky, rising from the soil, pressing in from the dark beyond the canopy. Silent, windless, patient, as if the realm had drawn a breath and refused to release it.
Alexios and Elisabeth reached for their swords before their minds caught up.
Isveth let out a strangled breath as her knees buckled. She caught herself on Myrasyn's arm, and Myrasyn, rigid with the effort of remaining upright, barely managed to do so.
Quinlan's girls stood easy. They'd felt this before.
The luminous leaves dimmed.
The pink light in the vines deepened. The stars, still recovering from their earlier blackout, burned a fraction brighter. The grass beneath his feet deepened in color, as if the soil itself exhaled.
At the base of the tree, a throne of braided vine and dark bark materialized from the roots, and on it a woman with one leg crossed over the other and her fingers draped along the armrest.
Demonic markings glowed steady across her skin, pulsing in time with the vines behind her, and the clothes that clung to her frame left very little to interpretation and nothing to modesty.
Nyxara rose.
The motion was smooth and unhurried, yet the weight in the air doubled as she left the throne, then tripled with the first step she took down the slope.
Alexios's vision tunneled.

"Jasmine is a good girl..." Serika chuckled.
"She's also very weak without her summons..."
Mimi only shook her head in response frantically and hid even further behind her sister.
"There's two of these wonderful existences?!" Isveth yelped.
Myrasyn was no better.
"And she's even smaller than Rosie?!
My heart will melt...!"
Then the pressure arrived.
It came from everywhere at once, falling from the sky, rising from the soil, pressing in from the dark beyond the canopy.
Silent, windless, patient, as if the realm had drawn a breath and refused to release it.
Alexios and Elisabeth reached for their swords before their minds caught up.
Isveth let out a strangled breath as her knees buckled.
She caught herself on Myrasyn's arm, and Myrasyn, rigid with the effort of remaining upright, barely managed to do so.
Quinlan's girls stood easy.
They'd felt this before.
The luminous leaves dimmed.
The pink light in the vines deepened.
The stars, still recovering from their earlier blackout, burned a fraction brighter.
The grass beneath his feet deepened in color, as if the soil itself exhaled.
At the base of the tree, a throne of braided vine and dark bark materialized from the roots, and on it a woman with one leg crossed over the other and her fingers draped along the armrest.
Demonic markings glowed steady across her skin, pulsing in time with the vines behind her, and the clothes that clung to her frame left very little to interpretation and nothing to modesty.
Nyxara rose.
The motion was smooth and unhurried, yet the weight in the air doubled as she left the throne, then tripled with the first step she took down the slope.
Alexios's vision tunneled.

chapters.title: Chapter 1792 An Ominous Existence
paragraphs: His breathing went shallow and fast, the old warrior's lungs seizing against a pressure his body read as being crushed alive, and his sword cleared its scabbard in one smooth motion.
"Father, I'll take its attention, you attack from a blind spot!" Elisabeth shouted, going from the pissy woman to the famed Dawn Breaker in a single breath.
Behind the two humans, Myrasyn was forming a spell circle. "She barely wears any armor, aim for her vitals! We have to kill her quickly!"
Isveth meanwhile began prowling to the right, looking to get around the terrible creature and attack from behind.
Nyxara took another step.
Alexios staggered.
His front knee nearly gave, and the grunt that left him was involuntary and furious, the thousand-year-old king who refused to kneel, though his body had stopped asking for his opinion.
Nyxara took a third step, and the stars above them went dark.

For one suffocating moment the realm held nothing but the sound of breathing and the demon descending, her expression idle and untroubled while four of the continent's strongest fell apart around her.
Then she stopped before Quinlan. The stars returned, the pressure halved, and the four newcomers sucked air like drowning swimmers breaking surface.

The most overwhelming presence any of them had ever felt sank to both knees, pressed a palm to her chest, and bowed her head to the Primordial Villain in a gesture so old that no culture in the realm could claim its origin.
"My Ruin." The warmth of embers in an ancient hearth. "Welcome back."
The silence that followed lived in the kind of space reserved for temples.
Alexios's grip on his sword had gone white.
Elisabeth tried to speak. Nothing came out.
"W-what?" Myrasyn breathed out carefully, composure holding her level by force, and managed, "What's going on? What exactly is she?"
"Thalorind's biggest slut," Vex answered before anyone else could.
Nyxara turned to the white-haired Hexwitch, and the giggle that left her was warm and dark and full of unfinished history.
"My little leech has quite the big mouth." No anger in it. Only promise. "We'll talk."
Kitsara was next.
"You too, foxy."
Every one of Kitsara's tails went rigid, and panic won the war against bravado before the tremor reached her ears. "W-what about the elf?! She also-"
"I have a name," Seraphiel murmured.
"Kukuku..." The sound came from low in Nyxara's chest, rich and patient. Her gaze passed over all three of them. "I shared my power with the sinfully curvy elf willingly..."
The smile widened. "But you two... Kukuku..."

Then the succubus straightened to full height, and her posture shifted, ceremonial. "But that's for later. My name is Nyxara, they call me the Primordial Demon of Lust. I'm the most dedicated lover of Quinlan Elysiar."
"Hah?" Vex's red stare went dead still, and the smirk vanished.
What replaced it was the territorial calm that preceded very bad decisions. "What did you just say?"
That was her throne this demon bitch was claiming.

Alexios's chest seized. For a dangerous second the strongest human alive felt he might truly suffer a heart attack. 'This is what the bastard was warning me about. Thought he said it because of the environment...'
Then his expression turned as sour as ever. 'His lover. This monster?'
"A Primordial? Does that mean...?!"
Nyxara vanished.
One moment she was in front of Quinlan, and the next the space was empty, and the pressure rematerialized directly behind Myrasyn.
Every muscle in the elven queen's body locked, every survival instinct screaming that the thing behind her could end her existence between one heartbeat and the next.
But instead, two arms slid around her from behind, slow and deliberate, settling low on her belly and drawing inward with an intimacy that made several women present shift where they stood.

"Yes, a primordial. I am a being like the woman you worship, Luminara," Nyxara whispered against the elf's ear, and the warmth of it made Myrasyn's skin prickle from her neck to her wrists. "I am the progenitor of demons."
"Like Luminara?!" Elisabeth's shout cracked through the air.
It took everything Alexios had not to break out into a cursing spree. 'A lover on this level...?! What does he not have?!'
Nyxara's lips shifted closer to Myrasyn's ear, and the whisper dropped into a register that made the queen squirm where she stood like never before.
"Yes... like Luminara. Just a lot sexier and much more fun." A pause came, intimate, dripping with amusement. "By the way... I saw what happened in the cell."
"You wretched demon, stop badmouthing the First Elf!" Myrasyn shouted, defiant.
But at the same time, she went scarlet from the roots of her hair to the tips of her long ears, and every shred of regal bearing evaporated in a single heartbeat. "And nothing happened in that cell!"
"I've been meaning to ask. What happened in that cell, exactly?" Lucille purred, curious and not even trying to hide how much she was enjoying this.
"I said, nothing!" Myrasyn stomped and squealed at once.
"'Stop badmouthing the First Elf, hmm...?'" Nyxara's smile sharpened.
"Have you ever wondered," she murmured against Myrasyn's twitching ear, "why you call her the 'First Elf' and not the 'First Female Elf?'"
Myrasyn and Isveth froze at the exact same instant, and the silence that followed was the loudest thing in the realm.

"Kukuku... How adorable..." Nyxara's tongue slid out, long and unmistakably inhuman, and Myrasyn's wide stare followed it despite every fiber of her dignity telling her not to. "By the way, if you ever need someone to coach your technique," the arms tightened a fraction on her belly, "just let me know." She leaned closer. "Lady Nyxara will show you the ropes of womanhood..."
Myrasyn achieved a shade of red that elven biology was never designed to produce.
"Stop molesting my elven ally, you damned demon."
Quinlan's tone landed cold and level, and Nyxara's composure broke in a full-body shudder.
"Yes, my love!"

The arms released Myrasyn instantly, and the Primordial Demon of Lust crossed the grass in a blur of pure devotion, arriving at the throne she was sitting in and pivoting to present it with both palms and a lowered stare.
"Please take your rightful seat."
Alexios watched the most powerful entity he had ever encountered rush to obey a man much, much weaker than her. She'd chosen her place long ago, and she'd never looked back.
He turned to Quinlan, and his voice came out hoarse. "You could have said a bit more than 'take a deep breath.'"
"Where's the fun in that? I was curious if your body still had full control at your ancient age," Quinlan replied nonchalantly as he walked to the throne and sat down.
He settled into the braided vine and dark bark, one arm on the armrest, his posture easy, and the realm responded.

The pink light in the vines pulsed brighter. The stars, still recovering from their earlier blackout, burned a fraction brighter. The grass beneath his feet deepened in color, as if the soil itself exhaled.
Nyxara watched him take the seat, and the ancient regal composure she'd been wearing dissolved like frost on warm glass.
"...Can I?"
She blinked at him, slow and devastating, fingers laced behind her back, weight shifting from one foot to the other, pleading.
Quinlan sighed.
"Come."
Nyxara landed in his lap before the word finished leaving his mouth, curling against his chest with a purr that vibrated through the throne and into the roots beneath it.
She nestled close, tucking her head under his chin, pressing herself into him with shameless heat, and her body offered every invitation a succubus could offer a man without saying a single word.
But Quinlan merely rested one hand on her thigh and the other on the armrest, and did nothing else.
The progenitor of the lust demons hummed louder.
"...You know why I'm here," he said.
The sound stopped.
"You always do this!" Nyxara pulled back just enough to look up at him, and the devastation on her face could have ended wars.

"You only come to see me when you need something! Do you know how lonely it is in here?! I decorated! I made the sky pretty! I painted Mimi's nails! And you show up and the first thing out of your mouth is 'Woman! Know your place! Do what I want, when I want, then shut it!'"
"I never said that."

"You basically did!" She buried her face back into his chest, squirming against him with a petulant fury that accomplished the exact opposite of protest, and the masochist in her was clearly, visibly, unmistakably savoring every second of being ignored in favor of business.
The assembled group watched the Primordial Demon of Lust throw a tantrum in the lap of her conqueror, and the looks on their faces ranged from wry familiarity to complete psychological collapse.
"Stop whining."
"But..." Nyxara kept on whimpering, looking greatly wronged.
Quinlan sighed, reached into his pocket ring, and drew the obsidian blade.
He held it up between them as he said, "I need your help getting the thing inside this to talk."
Her fingers reached for the blade, and the moment they made contact, the bubbly girlfriend and the whiny lover were gone.
Her touch traced the obsidian edge from hilt to tip, slow and clinical, and her eyes changed.
The playfulness bled out of them, replaced by a look that was unfathomably vast and old.

"I was careful back then," she murmured, turning the blade in her fingers with deliberate precision, examining a wound she'd inflicted. "I broke its will, but I left the pieces where they fell." Her lips curved, and the smile held nothing warm. "We just need to drag it back out."
She reached up toward Quinlan, gave his cheek a long, loud, and wet smooch, then the eyes of the Primordial Demon of Lust met the Primordial Villain's.
The look they exchanged was one of two apex predators getting ready to finish what they started.
"Let us begin."

chapters.title: Chapter 1793 Hunting a Will
paragraphs: Nyxara shifted in his lap.

One smooth motion, thighs pivoting, the blade transferring from her right hand to her left as she turned to face him fully, and when she settled back down her knees bracketed his hips and her eyes were level with his from inches away.
The obsidian relic hung loose in her left grip. Her right rose and pressed flat against the living metal covering his chest.
"Synchra, be a good girl and give me some room."
[Synchra] resisted for exactly one heartbeat, the Anima-grade armor humming a vibration against Nyxara's palm that carried more jealousy than compliance.
Then the living metal receded from his chest in a slow, grudging retreat, peeling back until warm skin met warm palm and the bond beneath it pulsed in recognition.
Nyxara's fingers spread over his heart, and her smile sharpened.
"What is she doing?!" Myrasyn yelped at the nearest person who looked like they might have answers, which happened to be Black Fang. "This woman is far too indecent!"
"She's a demon of lust," Black Fang replied with a perfect poker face.
"S-still! She has such a big audience! Has she no shame?!"
"Shame?" Black Fang's voice did not gain a single iota of emotion as she decreed, "She enjoys being watched."
"Eh!!" Myrasyn gasped. The innocent elven queen struggled to understand just how big of a pervert some women could be.
Isveth's ears were twitching at a frequency that suggested mechanical failure.
Elisabeth had turned away, her neck flushed to the collar. "Demons are truly obscene creatures..." she muttered under her breath. "No wonder she likes him so much..."
Serika's hands came down over Mimi's eyes from behind. The little dryad squirmed instantly, batting at the fingers. "Big sis Serika I want to see!!"
"You can't."
"Not fair!"
Alexios stood still as he took stock of what had just happened in the last few minutes.
He'd stepped through a portal into a separate dimension, met a demon on par with the elven legend, and nearly drawn steel on a being that could have erased him between breaths.
And now, the thousand-year-old King of the Vraven Kingdom was watching the aforementioned creature of terror straddle a man on a throne of living vine, acting like a maiden in love.
He exhaled through his nose and looked at the grass.
Nyxara's palm pressed a fraction deeper against Quinlan's heart. "Hold me tightly."
"Is that necessary?" Quinlan asked, suspecting foul play.
"Absolutely."
Just the word, plain and unadorned, and the ancient gaze behind it had stopped performing.
"Alright. I'm ready." His arms wrapped around her waist, and Nyxara closed her eyes.
"Let's begin then, my beloved Ruin."
Every demonic sigil, every winding pink line from her collarbones to her hips, blazed at once.
The light that poured off her was heavy and old, older than the relic in her grip by eons, and it carried a resonance that made the roots of the soul realm's tree curl tighter into the soil.
Her touch burned with presence rather than heat, reaching past skin and bone to press against a depth that had no physical location but answered to her all the same.
In her left, the blade began to hum.
It was a thin, miserable sound, nothing like the furious hunger that had torn through his veins in the arena. This was the noise of a broken will recognizing what had shattered it.
Through the bond Quinlan felt Nyxara reach, but the direction wasn't the same as last time.
Back then, the blade invaded him, and she appeared to squash the bug who dared attack her tired lover.

Now, she was pushing outward through the hand that held the blade, using his heart as the anchor and the relic as the door, forcing her way into the broken space inside the obsidian where the fragments of its will had retreated after she shattered them.
Her hand curled tighter against his chest, pulling at skin, and the markings on her body flared brighter.
Quinlan watched her face from inches away while she worked, and a quiet recognition turned over inside him.

The shameless seductress who threw tantrums in his lap and begged for attention had given way to a woman pouring everything she had into a task because he needed it done, her focus absolute, her power vast yet careful entirely for his sake.
The way her lip caught between her teeth when she reached deeper, the small unconscious lean of her body into his as though proximity was a resource she couldn't afford to waste.
'...You really are a good woman, aren't you?'
A smile touched his mouth, warm and unhurried, and he pulled her fully against him, one arm tight around her waist, the other bracing the back of her head until his brow rested against hers.

The channel widened. His will joined hers, flowing through the bond and into the relic together, and the inside of the blade resolved around them the way a dark room does when you adjust to the dimness.
It was a cramped, dead space, lightless and old, and everything in it reeked of starvation.
And in that space, something flinched.
The fragments scattered.
They bolted in every direction at once, shards of a will that had devoured mortals for sport now fleeing like insects from a lifted stone, and every single one of them ran from Nyxara.
She didn't give chase in the traditional sense. There was no tag being played today.

Instead, she expanded, flooding outward through the relic's inner space in a slow, patient tide, closing off the corners they fled toward one by one, and the fragments recoiled from each sealed exit and scrambled toward the only direction she hadn't claimed.
Toward him.
Quinlan was already there.

Instinct answered before conscious thought did, and his will closed around them like a fist around a handful of sand. The fragments thrashed against the grip, screeching in frequencies that had no sound, clawing at the walls of his intent with the desperation of a mind that understood it had been herded.
Nyxara pressed in from every other side, patient and immense.
And just like that, the fragments went still.
Between the two of them, pinned inside the relic with nowhere left to run, the broken shards of the blade's consciousness shuddered and began to cohere.
Pieces finding pieces, edges grinding together, a will reassembling itself just enough to think, just enough to know where it was and who held it.
'...That's it?'
What reassembled was pathetic. A thin, trembling presence with the memory of hunger but none of the teeth.
Nyxara's grip tightened around it, and the chase was over.
They opened their eyes at the same time.
Nyxara was already looking at him, hazy and half-lidded, drunk on what they'd just shared.
She had reached into the deepest part of his existence and felt his will move alongside hers.
Her breath came shallow against his lips, her fingers still curled against his chest, and the flush across her demonic markings pulsed in slow, heavy waves that made the air between them feel thick.
"Loving you," she whispered, raw and stripped past every layer of performance and ancient composure she wore, "is a stronger high than anything this world has ever produced."
Quinlan's mouth curved, and he answered her in a language older than words.
He kissed her.
Nyxara melted into him instantly, her fingers sliding from his chest to the back of his neck, pulling him deeper.
"Mmmm~" The sounds she made against his mouth were shameless and entirely, devastatingly her.

The bond between them blazed wide open, and through it Nyxara released what they'd caught, pushing the reassembled consciousness down through the connection, through his vessel, through the palm still pressed between them, and into the blade resting in her other grip.
The relic shuddered.

The obsidian edge lost its black. Color bled out of the metal in a slow, exhausted drain until the blade hung grey and dull in Nyxara's grip, and a faint, wretched pulse of awareness throbbed inside it like a heartbeat that didn't want to exist.
Behind them, Myrasyn achieved a shade of pink that rivaled Nyxara's markings, and Isveth's ears had stopped twitching entirely in what appeared to be a full system shutdown.
Nyxara pulled back.
"Pah..." The sound was wet and shameless, lingering far longer than any kiss in front of an audience had a right to.
She then looked at the grey blade in her grip, and ordered,
"Speak."
The word carried the weight of the bond behind it, Quinlan's vessel as the anchor and Nyxara's will as the leash, and the grey blade pulsed once, twice, and then a voice emerged from the metal.

He'd stepped through a portal into a separate dimension, met a demon on par with the elven legend, and nearly drawn steel on a being that could have erased him between breaths.
And now, the thousand-year-old King of the Vraven Kingdom was watching the aforementioned creature of terror straddle a man on a throne of living vine, acting like a maiden in love.
He exhaled through his nose and looked at the grass.
Nyxara's palm pressed a fraction deeper against Quinlan's heart.
"Hold me tightly."
"Is that necessary?" Quinlan asked, suspecting foul play.
"Absolutely."
Just the word, plain and unadorned, and the ancient gaze behind it had stopped performing.
"Alright.
I'm ready." His arms wrapped around her waist, and Nyxara closed her eyes.
"Let's begin then, my beloved Ruin."
Every demonic sigil, every winding pink line from her collarbones to her hips, blazed at once.
The light that poured off her was heavy and old, older than the relic in her grip by eons, and it carried a resonance that made the roots of the soul realm's tree curl tighter into the soil.
Her touch burned with presence rather than heat, reaching past skin and bone to press against a depth that had no physical location but answered to her all the same.
In her left, the blade began to hum.
It was a thin, miserable sound, nothing like the furious hunger that had torn through his veins in the arena.
This was the noise of a broken will recognizing what had shattered it.
Through the bond Quinlan felt Nyxara reach, but the direction wasn't the same as last time.
Back then, the blade invaded him, and she appeared to squash the bug who dared attack her tired lover.

Now, she was pushing outward through the hand that held the blade, using his heart as the anchor and the relic as the door, forcing her way into the broken space inside the obsidian where the fragments of its will had retreated after she shattered them.
Her hand curled tighter against his chest, pulling at skin, and the markings on her body flared brighter.
Quinlan watched her face from inches away while she worked, and a quiet recognition turned over inside him.

The shameless seductress who threw tantrums in his lap and begged for attention had given way to a woman pouring everything she had into a task because he needed it done, her focus absolute, her power vast yet careful entirely for his sake.
The way her lip caught between her teeth when she reached deeper, the small unconscious lean of her body into his as though proximity was a resource she couldn't afford to waste.
'...You really are a good woman, aren't you?'
A smile touched his mouth, warm and unhurried, and he pulled her fully against him, one arm tight around her waist, the other bracing the back of her head until his brow rested against hers.
The channel widened.
His will joined hers, flowing through the bond and into the relic together, and the inside of the blade resolved around them the way a dark room does when you adjust to the dimness.
It was a cramped, dead space, lightless and old, and everything in it reeked of starvation.
And in that space, something flinched.
The fragments scattered.
They bolted in every direction at once, shards of a will that had devoured mortals for sport now fleeing like insects from a lifted stone, and every single one of them ran from Nyxara.
She didn't give chase in the traditional sense.
There was no tag being played today.

Instead, she expanded, flooding outward through the relic's inner space in a slow, patient tide, closing off the corners they fled toward one by one, and the fragments recoiled from each sealed exit and scrambled toward the only direction she hadn't claimed.
Toward him.
Quinlan was already there.
Instinct answered before conscious thought did, and his will closed around them like a fist around a handful of sand.
The fragments thrashed against the grip, screeching in frequencies that had no sound, clawing at the walls of his intent with the desperation of a mind that understood it had been herded.
Nyxara pressed in from every other side, patient and immense.
And just like that, the fragments went still.
Between the two of them, pinned inside the relic with nowhere left to run, the broken shards of the blade's consciousness shuddered and began to cohere.
Pieces finding pieces, edges grinding together, a will reassembling itself just enough to think, just enough to know where it was and who held it.
'...That's it?'
What reassembled was pathetic.
A thin, trembling presence with the memory of hunger but none of the teeth.
Nyxara's grip tightened around it, and the chase was over.
They opened their eyes at the same time.
Nyxara was already looking at him, hazy and half-lidded, drunk on what they'd just shared.
She had reached into the deepest part of his existence and felt his will move alongside hers.
Her breath came shallow against his lips, her fingers still curled against his chest, and the flush across her demonic markings pulsed in slow, heavy waves that made the air between them feel thick.
"Loving you," she whispered, raw and stripped past every layer of performance and ancient composure she wore, "is a stronger high than anything this world has ever produced."
Quinlan's mouth curved, and he answered her in a language older than words.
He kissed her.
Nyxara melted into him instantly, her fingers sliding from his chest to the back of his neck, pulling him deeper.
"Mmmm~" The sounds she made against his mouth were shameless and entirely, devastatingly her.

The bond between them blazed wide open, and through it Nyxara released what they'd caught, pushing the reassembled consciousness down through the connection, through his vessel, through the palm still pressed between them, and into the blade resting in her other grip.
The relic shuddered.
The obsidian edge lost its black.

Color bled out of the metal in a slow, exhausted drain until the blade hung grey and dull in Nyxara's grip, and a faint, wretched pulse of awareness throbbed inside it like a heartbeat that didn't want to exist.
Behind them, Myrasyn achieved a shade of pink that rivaled Nyxara's markings, and Isveth's ears had stopped twitching entirely in what appeared to be a full system shutdown.
Nyxara pulled back.
"Pah..." The sound was wet and shameless, lingering far longer than any kiss in front of an audience had a right to.
She then looked at the grey blade in her grip, and ordered,
"Speak."
The word carried the weight of the bond behind it, Quinlan's vessel as the anchor and Nyxara's will as the leash, and the grey blade pulsed once, twice, and then a voice emerged from the metal.

chapters.title: Chapter 1794 The Blade's Truth
paragraphs: A thin wet rasp responded. It managed one word.
"No?" Quinlan raised an eyebrow from his throne of braided vine, Nyxara still warm against his chest.
After dealing with Chizuru's nonsense longer than he should have, Quinlan tried the obvious next.
"[Subjugation]." The spell left him clean, aimed at the consciousness inside the blade, and caught nothing.
Like closing a fist around smoke. Not enough of an entity left to bind.
'...Great.'

His eyes found Nyxara's, and the nod he gave her was small. The leash tightened through the bond. The blade screamed, thin and pitiful, and when she eased off the wretched thing cringed so hard it nearly came apart. "I wasn't asking. Speak the truth, only the truth, or you'll forever regret opposing me."
Three heartbeats of silence. Then the rasp returned. "...What do you want to know?"
"What exactly are you?" Quinlan asked.

Nyxara didn't need to squeeze. Her attention drifted toward the blade, idle, and the answer spilled before the pressure arrived. "...A key. To borders. Thresholds. I was forged to cut even what should not be possible to cut." The rasp steadied. "Severing is my purpose."
The pulse in the grey metal flickered, a fraction dimmer than when it first spoke.
"Where did the Fujimori come from?" Ayame's tone was the second-in-command's, composed and precise.

The blade strained. Quinlan could feel it through Nyxara, the wretched thing reaching for memories that dissolved before they formed. "A continent east of here... They were powerful... once. Driven from their homeland, invaded. Defeated."
"What invaded them?" Black Fang asked.
"Enemies..." The rasp died. When it returned, it was thinner. "I don't remember everything. The years in the dark were long. I wasn't created to store information but to sever."
"Could it also be because of what the demoness did to you?" Vex lobbed the accusation, aimed squarely at the woman in her man's lap.

Nyxara sighed, a theatrical exhale, eyes closed, chin tilting skyward. "Jealousy is such an ugly trait in a woman... I shattered its will, not its memory. Cleanly, precisely, every piece left exactly where it fell."
She concluded with a scoff. "I don't make mistakes, little leech."

"So the Fujimori of old ran from their homeland and arrived in Iskaris. How did they get through the barrier? No one else entered before or after them as far as our records indicate." Alexios broke through the female banter.
"I slit the edge..." A grinding pause, trying to remember the details. "They sacrificed their people at the wall to empower me... And I made a wound large enough for the clan to pass through."
Myrasyn's ears went rigid. "Does that mean you can cut through it again? Can we leave if we power you up again?"
"No."
"Why not?" Aurora prompted.

"Because getting in is easier than leaving. But even if it wasn't, you wretches of Iskaris are so pitifully weak I'd require your whole population sacrificed twice over to harvest that much strength."
"..." Being belittled like that, for once, sounded more ominous than mocking. Quinlan and co were used to being treated as the underdogs, but what this thing was saying...
Just how powerful were the people on the outside?
"So you cut through the barrier. Then what?" Ayame kept her eyes on the blade, where the grey pulse had slowed to a crawl.
"Everyone who crossed above the seventy-fourth threshold died within minutes."

'Fuck...' Quinlan cursed, having a bad premonition. This sounded far too close to what Vasilen Sangomar, the ancient vampire, had told Quinlan. The archduke managed to survive, but he did so as a heavily suppressed existence.
The blade confirmed his thoughts.

"Hmm... Oh, yes. I remember. The domain you clueless barbarians call the 'Heavenly Restriction' killed them... Their cores could not sustain themselves against the drain. The strongest, the ones who could have led, including my wielder..."
The rasp went thin. "They suffocated where they stood..."
Alexios's jaw tightened.
"The clan arrived with its head cut off," Quinlan murmured.
"That'd explain why even the elders are so clueless," Ayame sighed.
"Driven from their homeland in a hurry..." Lucille shook her head, disappointed.
"The only clan records that could've survived, including the elders' 'instructions from the ancestors,' were written by weak followers, not leaders," Black Fang concluded.
"How much stronger were these ancestors than I am? What was their level?" Alexios asked.
"...You'd not even be worthy of cleaning their boots, boy king. As for their level... I don't remember."
"Was it over a hundred?" Serika inquired.
"Yes."
"Over two hundred?"
"...I don't remember."
"One fifty?"
"I don't know..."
"..." Serika sighed, disappointed but happy she at least got confirmation of the outsiders being more than level one hundred.
Which in itself had grave implications for all denizens of Iskaris.
"It's fading." Aurora watched the blade, clinical. The grey pulse that had answered Nyxara's command was guttering, each throb weaker and farther apart than the last.
Nyxara glanced down at the blade in her grip without lifting her head from Quinlan's chest. "I forced it to speak to us, but this isn't its natural state of being."

Her grip shifted on the hilt. "I'm not only keeping it conscious without becoming its wielder, but I'm also forcing it to speak. It's like sustaining a flame where there is no air. It won't last much longer."
"I see..." Aurora nodded. "Thank you for the explanation."
"What's there to thank? I just answered my sister-wife's question~" Nyxara purred, drawing a heart on Quinlan's skin.

Isveth observed the demoness for a long moment, braving herself for the disrespect she was about to show toward one of the Holy Son's women, then spoke up. "Forgive me, but Miss Demon is from beyond the Restriction, is she not? Surely she knows more than this corrupt sword spirit thing can offer."
The response she received was far different than whatever the elf could've ever expected.
Nyxara turned her face into Quinlan's neck, hiding, and the words came out bare and small. "I'm sorry, my love..."
Quinlan's hand settled on her head, fingers moving through her hair with extreme gentleness, and he addressed the room without looking up. "She's restricted in what she can tell me."
Myrasyn opened her mouth, looked at the primordial demon nuzzling into her boyfriend's neck with droopy eyes and the posture of a kicked puppy, and closed it again.
"Ah..." Isveth hurriedly bowed. "I'm sorry, Miss Demon."
Nyxara didn't respond, instead electing to hide further away into her conqueror.
Quinlan turned back to the fading blade.
"The Fujimori were running. If they had to run, they weren't the strongest beings out there. How strong is Thalorind's peak, then?"
The blade took a long time to answer. When the rasp returned, it was barely audible, each word surfacing at a cost.
"The ones who... defeated them." A long, grinding silence. "The gap between you and the peak... Is unfathomable..."
"Give me concretes. How much stronger are they?"
"...I don't know."
For a long, long second, nobody spoke as Quinlan's hand went still on Nyxara's back.
Across the clearing, Alexios was looking at him, and for the first time, both men were truly speechless at the same time.
The implications of what this thing revealed thus far have been overwhelming.
But the blade was fading, and they couldn't afford to stop.
"You called the Heavenly Restriction a 'domain' earlier." Black Fang spoke up, cutting through the quiet. "Not a barrier. Explain."
The pulse in the grey metal skipped. For a moment Quinlan thought it had stopped entirely, then it returned, weaker.

"A domain is... a will. Someone's..." The rasp fragmented, reformed. "...will, laid over the land... and its people. Authority. A ruler's... claim. The seal around this continent... belongs to someone."
Elisabeth, who hadn't looked back since Nyxara's display, turned toward the blade.
"Who is this 'ruler?'" Alexios's voice was very quiet.
"I... don't remember..." The rasp had gone thin as thread.

"You told the Fujimori that conquering Iskaris would bring about the golden age of the clan. Kaede told the Scarlet Lilies that if they helped her win Greenvale - which was the first step toward conquering the continent - she could bring down the Heavenly Restriction," Ayame spoke up at last. "These two must be connected. Explain."
The rasp came back thinner than ever before.
"Yes... It is connected... Cause and effect... A domain belongs to... the one who drew it. And a domain can be... challenged. By a claim of equal standing."
The words were dissolving between syllables now. "If a new ruler rises... and the land answers... the original claim... will not hold."

"Explain the mechanics properly. Stop speaking in riddles." Quinlan had had enough. "What counts as conquering? What are the effects of a domain exactly? Can a so-called ruler just cast a domain or dispel one at will?"
"Kekeke... Little primordial... My sincerest of apologies, but... I... Don't... Remember..."
The grey metal pulsed once more and went still.
The thin presence Nyxara had forced into coherence scattered back into the depths of the blade, leaving behind a crowd too stunned to even speak from all the implications they'd just learned.
Well, save for the old king.
"Fuck me."

chapters.title: Chapter 1795 Crushing Implications
paragraphs: Quinlan watched the grey blade go dark in Nyxara's palm, and nobody in the soul realm spoke for a long time.
Overhead, the stars burned in their uncharted patterns, dense and motionless.

Pink light pulsed from the tree at the heart of the realm into roots that curled deeper into the soil, and even that faint glow seemed to have dimmed since the blade's last words. The air carried no wind, and the silence that settled over the clearing pressed down on everyone standing in it with a weight that had nothing to do with gravity.
The implications of what was revealed felt...
Crippling.
Alexios's breathing had gone shallow. The old king stood with one hand white-knuckled on his sword hilt, staring at the grass.
His kingdom, his throne, his wars and treaties and careful rule, all of it had existed inside a cage drawn by someone else's will.
Ayame hadn't moved. Her composure held, but her gaze had gone distant, already parsing the blade's last words for a thread they could pull.
The rest of them wore the weight just as heavily. Nobody in the clearing had shifted their stance since the blade went silent.
But at the same time, nobody crumbled either.
These were the continent's biggest risk-takers, and learning the continent was a cage didn't change what they were.

But still... Dealing with the revelation that nearly every assumption they'd walked in with had just been unmade... The silence was crushing enough that even Quinlan let it sit longer than he should have.

He stared at the dead blade in Nyxara's grip, and for a few seconds the sheer enormity of what the wretched thing had said pressed in from every direction: an entire continent under someone's will and a world that would treat the lot of them like insects.
Then he shut it down.
*Clap!*
The sound cracked through the clearing, and every eye snapped to him.
"Alright. We've learned some heavy information, but so what?"

Quinlan smiled, confident, examining his girls one by one. "We've been underdogs all our lives. From the moment you met me, to this very point, there was never a time when we could declare ourselves supreme."
"..." Kaelira, Kitsara, Lucille, all of them were listening to him speak with utmost focus. The way he spoke to them was an anchor, plain and simple.

Quinlan's smile deepened. "We always knew that Iskaris was only the beginning, that there were much stronger beings out there. What we really need to discuss is how to proceed, how to maneuver so we go from 'insects' to beings that no outsider can squash."
The tension in the clearing shifted, and the faces watching him had traded weight for focus.

"The Restriction is somebody's will over the continent, and it can be challenged by a so-called ruler." He settled deeper into the throne, one arm still around Nyxara. "That's the part that matters. Everything else is just context."
His gaze swept the clearing and landed on Alexios.
"So let's figure out what 'ruler' means and how we proceed."
"Hubby's right."
Vex walked toward the throne without hurrying, red eyes sweeping the clearing.

"The Heavenly Restriction has been sitting here for hundreds of thousands of years. If whoever drew it planned to come back and collect, they'd have done it already." She stopped in front of the throne, considered the lap situation, and chose Quinlan's unoccupied thigh.

She sat down, shifted until she found a comfortable angle, and pulled Quinlan's free arm around her waist before he could object. Nyxara, nudged aside by the possessive motion, let out a quiet giggle that promised future consequences.
"The chances of that changing while we're standing here are basically zero," Vex continued. "We have time to figure this out, so let's do exactly that."

"Easy for you to say." Elisabeth's voice cut in from the side, her stare fixed on Quinlan. "'We always knew Iskaris was just the beginning?' Speak for yourself. Some of us just learned the world we lived our entire lives in is a prison. We had no idea that there were stronger beings out there, save for the Goddess."
Vex's red stare slid to the Dawn Breaker without her head moving. "And? Stop taking that tone with my husband, woman. He can't be blamed for your lack of information."
"..." Elisabeth remained silent for a few seconds before she said, "I'm not blaming anyone, I'm just saying that moving on isn't so easy for everyone."
"Oh, okay." Vex nodded along, saintly. "Why don't you hold your father's hand for stability, then?"
Elisabeth's eyes widened. "What did you just say?"
"Vex..." Quinlan chuckled, and his hand came up to rest on top of Vex's head. His fingers moved through her white hair once, and the Hexwitch's entire posture softened under the touch.

"...Sorry, Hubby." Vex's voice dropped, the edge gone as quickly as it had arrived. She glanced up at him. "I just hate it when these hypocrites keep speaking to you as if you were to blame for everything."
Elisabeth stared at her. "...Why are you apologizing to him?"
"I know, I know..." Quinlan sighed at his Hexwitch. "But now more than ever we should try to work together with even the church, no matter how bad they get on our nerves."
"Hmph..." The Dawn Breaker seemed beyond dissatisfied.
"Elisabeth Valorian." Quinlan spoke up, and the shift in his tone made the Arch Priestess straighten where she stood.
"I know full well how you feel. Believe it or not, I was born with even less information and guidance than you were."
Elisabeth frowned. "What about your mother, Luminara?"

Quinlan reached up and grabbed his own ear, pulling. "She's my adoptive mother, and I didn't meet her until I reached the second bottleneck. When I first started out, I was a newborn primordial, alone, with zero information about how anything in this world worked. I didn't know what a level meant, or XP, or classes. Nothing."
"Alone?!" Myrasyn's ears went rigid. Isveth's hand pressed to her chest as though she'd been struck.
They knew he was an adoptive son as he'd already admitted that much, explaining why he didn't look elven despite being Luminara's child.
What the elves did not know is how he started out, how Luminara wasn't there from the beginning. He'd found her on his own, after surviving a world that gave him nothing.
'She must be so sad... Her poor child had to struggle alone without her being there to help him...' Myrasyn whimpered inwardly, feeling terrible for the First Elf.

"On day two of my journey, I met my stalwart samurai." Quinlan's gaze drifted to Ayame, warm. "Then my amazing dogkin." Blossom's tail wagged hard. "And then the rest, one by one. Together, we figured everything out, piece by piece."
He observed Elisabeth with none of his usual arrogance or mockery shown toward believers of what he openly called the hypocrite Goddess.

"Point is, we've all been in the dark at some point." A pause, and his voice lost its edge entirely. "I'm not your enemy, Elisabeth. None of us can afford that anymore. Let's get through this together, shall we?"
Across the clearing, Lucille caught Jasmine's eye, and the look that passed between them was brief and knowing.

Their husband was playing the role of a reasonable diplomat perfectly. He realized Elisabeth was struggling to come to terms with her new reality, finding its implications too crushing. Thus, he offered her a new set of information, high enough in its shock value to contend with everything else they learned, but not one bit as ominous.
Learning this new information about him only served to help the clearing move on, less dreadful of the future.
And just like that, the clearing shifted.
Elisabeth's posture loosened by a fraction, and the combative set of her shoulders eased. "...I forgive your foul-mouthed girlfriend for her naughty behavior."
Quinlan grinned and petted Vex once more in response. "Much appreciated."
"Hehe~" Vex leaned back against Quinlan's chest, tilted her head, and pressed a slow kiss to the side of his neck.
Then her red stare found Nyxara's across his lap.
The look that passed between the two women lasted less than a second, but it carried everything.
Vex's pride was quiet and absolute. She'd played the room's villain on purpose and watched her man walk in as the hero, exactly the way she'd set it up.

Nyxara's grin spread slow and warm, her ancient eyes dancing with amusement. She said nothing either, but the look she gave the Hexwitch was the closest thing to respect the Primordial Demon of Lust had ever offered her little leech.
Vex curled into Quinlan's side, and the Hexwitch's work was done.
"Shall we proceed, then?" Quinlan asked, and all of his guests looked ready to move on.
"The blade said the domain can be challenged by a ruler's claim." Black Fang wasted no time.
